nodes.label: Developer work-practices field study (not commercial report)
Software engineering begins before the code
nodes.summary: Begin with established evidence on how professional developers spend time understanding, modifying, testing and integrating systems. Distinguish typing a patch from delivering an accepted, operable change, then introduce agentic-software-engineering visions explicitly as proposed extensions rather than as measured proof.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: From autocomplete to delegated execution
nodes.summary: Introduce completion, conversational assistance, repository-aware agents and multi-step autonomous execution as progressively larger delegations. Explain which choices remain human-owned at each level and why increased autonomy changes coordination and control costs.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: The engineer's work before and after AI
nodes.summary: Describe the transfer of effort from typing and routine lookup toward problem framing, architecture, checking, integration and responsibility. Treat changes in developer activity as hypotheses to test, not as universal workforce predictions.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: The lifecycle of a trustworthy change
nodes.summary: Trace stakeholder intention, discovery, design options, implementation, independently specified checks, human review, deployment and feedback. Define the change dossier and responsible decision-maker at each handoff. This is the author's engineering reference workflow, motivated by software lifecycle evidence and agent-governance proposals rather than experimentally validated as a whole.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: The autonomy–accountability boundary
nodes.summary: Separate permission to act from authority to approve residual risk. Discuss human-on-the-loop and human-in-the-loop as design choices conditioned by impact and observability rather than slogans.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Why brownfield change starts with system comprehension
nodes.summary: Introduce the existing system's implicit invariants, distributed rationale and human ownership as prerequisites to a safe code edit. An early minimum context package must exist before Chapter 3 lets an agent inspect the repository; Chapter 9 will later explain how to preserve and update that knowledge durably.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: What the research can and cannot tell us
nodes.summary: Explain study types before citing effects: controlled experiments, repository observation, surveys, benchmarks, industrial reports and position papers. Distinguish observed measurements from recommended governance processes, preparing readers to interpret the evidence critically.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: A teaching case, not a reported field experiment
nodes.summary: Introduce the invented transaction-approval API, its legacy interfaces, ambiguous regional threshold request and audit obligations. Make the system boundary and synthetic data explicit. Ownership and review findings explain why the example is realistic; no cited paper is claimed to have studied this particular service.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: From generated output to an evidence question
nodes.summary: Summarize why the reader must ask what changed, how it was checked and what consequence followed. Define the initial questions to be answered in a controlled pilot and bridge to a rigorous discussion of productivity.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: The productivity denominator problem
nodes.summary: Explain why suggestions accepted, tokens generated, commits, pull requests, merged changes, releases and user outcomes form different denominators. Construct a funnel in which gains can disappear at review or integration.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: How to read causal evidence
nodes.summary: Teach random assignment, matched comparison, before/after measurements, selection effects and confidence intervals using developer-tool experiments. State what a reported percentage does and does not quantify.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Why controlled studies disagree
nodes.summary: Compare positive enterprise evidence with the slower results for experienced open-source maintainers, making task familiarity, tool era, environment and developer cohort explicit. The object is conditional understanding, not a synthesized universal multiplier.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Observational adoption and its confounders
nodes.summary: Examine repository adoption studies and agent trace analyses. Discuss parallel trend assumptions, tooling changes, self-selection, repository maturity and the limits of activity telemetry.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Writing code versus shipping code
nodes.summary: Introduce work in progress, review capacity, testing and release mechanisms as bottlenecks. Build a simple throughput model that explains why significantly more code and commits need not produce proportionately more deployed value.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Quality-adjusted productivity
nodes.summary: Treat complexity, post-merge rework, reviewer effort, rollback and incident risk as potential costs of faster output. Use longitudinal and maintenance studies as narrower empirical signals; position commercial industry reports as descriptive comparisons rather than causal estimates.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Developer experience and hidden time
nodes.summary: Compare measured task time with perceived savings, context switching, flow and debugging effort. Explain why surveys and tool dashboards are informative about adoption but insufficient for causal conclusions.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Designing a coding-specific field pilot
nodes.summary: Set up a preregistered experiment on comparable software-maintenance tasks with a fixed observation period, quality guardrails, reviewer-minute accounting, random assignment where feasible, and documented statistical power. Enterprise coding RCTs are direct precedents; an identity-administration RCT is useful only as a cross-domain illustration of experiment design.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: From metrics to an evidence-based pilot decision
nodes.summary: Combine measures of delivery, change failure, security, review load, human time and learning into a predeclared pilot scorecard, with uncertainty and stop criteria. DORA's ROI guide supplies practitioner calculation structure, not a new controlled-effect estimate; governance design is the author's proposed operational response.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: From suggestion to a permission-bounded agent
nodes.summary: Describe repository reads, plans, shell tools, patches, test execution and stateful observations, but establish workspace containment, synthetic fixtures, restricted shell and no production credentials *before* the first agent action. This minimal safe runtime is elaborated into a full threat model in Chapter 6.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: What an agent actually observes
nodes.summary: Distinguish source files, build outputs, test results, tool responses, retrieval context and missing organizational knowledge. Show how partial observation yields confident but incorrect modifications.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: The task envelope
nodes.summary: Define task size, blast radius, dependency coupling, domain novelty and availability of external checks. Propose routing rules for completion, supervised agent work or full human ownership rather than scaling autonomy blindly.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Agent benchmarks and observed pull requests
nodes.summary: Separate evaluation on constructed or selected tasks from naturally occurring GitHub agent PRs and from spectacular long-horizon demonstrations. Check task selection, contamination, pass criteria, human intervention and data lineage before translating any reported success into production reliability; MirrorCode is capability evidence, not a proven autonomous calendar-time SLA.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Common failure modes in real changes
nodes.summary: Organize failures into misunderstood requirements, inadequate context, API mismatch, build or dependency problems, speculative fixes and integration friction. Show why retries without a diagnosis can repeat the same error.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: A bounded propose–act–observe loop
nodes.summary: Build an explicit task state machine: intake, plan, limited tool actions, observation, independent check, budget exhaustion, handoff. Production coding traces and failed agent PRs motivate failure handling; deterministic orchestration results from non-SWE tool workflows are architectural analogies, not proof that this loop will succeed on brownfield tasks.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: When parallel agents help and hurt
nodes.summary: Explain decomposition of independent work, merge conflicts, overlapping context assumptions and correlated failures. Separate the theoretical appeal of parallelism from evidence about actual project throughput.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Stopping rules versus acceptance authority
nodes.summary: Explain local stopping, retry budgets, external failure signals and human escalation as an implementable policy. A passing test or a self-review earns readiness for independent review, not permission to deploy; specify a bounded fallback when two orchestrator rejections cannot cite a policy reason.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Agent capability as a testable hypothesis
nodes.summary: Close by specifying an observable candidate output, evidence required for acceptance and the human who owns remaining uncertainty. The gap between prompt and approved intent motivates specification-driven engineering.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Separate intention determination from design
nodes.summary: Introduce problem framing, stakeholder analysis, behavioral boundaries and unacceptable outcomes before asking for a solution. Explain how premature code generation anchors the team to an unvalidated interpretation of the request.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: From a request to a versioned intention ledger
nodes.summary: Show a lightweight ledger with stakeholder, desired outcome, assumptions, open questions, uncertainty, prohibitions and authoritative sign-off. Treat this ledger as the book's proposed agile practice; studies of OSS governance and agentic engineering motivate traceability, but do not validate this specific artifact.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: Write behavioral examples before implementation
nodes.summary: Turn stakeholder-approved outcomes into concrete examples, invariants, negative cases and backwards-compatibility constraints. Distinguish an independently confirmed rule from a specification docstring inferred by an LLM from code: the latter reduces some test misguidance in Zhao et al. but cannot establish that the inferred rule matches stakeholder intent.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Executable contracts without circular oracles
nodes.summary: Map authoritative examples to deterministic assertions, schemas, properties and negative tests. Explain the self-confirmation failure when generated tests copy faulty implementation behavior, and the limited mitigation reported by specification-based prompting. The authoritative acceptance oracle must be reviewed independently from the produced patch.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: Architecture decision versus acceptance contract
nodes.summary: Teach readers to keep the fixed intent separate from several candidate implementation designs. Design constraints can be negotiated, but changes to user-visible semantics require renewed authorization.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: A delta-driven iterative brownfield lifecycle
nodes.summary: Propose short cycles: examine the existing behavior, clarify and version the next intention delta, analyze design impact, implement one reversible slice, independently test, review, deploy and learn. Repository studies motivate the need for bounded changes, while FlowGen compares simulated Scrum/TDD/Waterfall processes on coding benchmarks—not real agile brownfield team outcomes.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: Late intentions and explicit impact analysis
nodes.summary: When a new regional requirement arrives after code exists, retain the previous intent revision; record who authorized the change, which design alternatives and checks it invalidates, and whether to amend, roll back or defer the implementation. Code-critique and OSS-policy observations motivate traceability; the delta/impact workflow is a proposed method rather than a measured benefit of those studies.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: Native intent gates and optional compatibility adapters
nodes.summary: Define native gates on approved intention, invariants, architecture decisions, verification evidence and acceptance authority. Keep a legacy user-story/test-case view as an optional adapter when integrating established CI, rather than treating it as canonical. Use the CCS profile as a worked engineering example, not a method empirically demonstrated by Farrag or Qiu.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: The approval-rule contract across two iterations
nodes.summary: Show a complete before/after trace of the fictional approval service: original ambiguity, an agreed acceptance contract, a first implementation delta, a late regional exception, the new contract revision and the test diff. Explicitly mark which artifacts are invented pedagogical examples and which limitations are informed by empirical work on intent drift and review.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: What counts as code quality?
nodes.summary: Establish correctness, readability, cohesion, coupling, duplication, complexity, changeability and operational reliability as separate dimensions. Explain why an all-purpose quality score obscures important trade-offs.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Reading AI-versus-human studies correctly
nodes.summary: Discuss code-unit selection, languages, code size, authorship inference, matched baselines and static-analysis definitions. Use conflicting results to demonstrate why no universal AI-code superiority or inferiority claim is warranted.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Code smells are signals, not incidents
nodes.summary: Separate static warnings, complexity growth and duplication from externally observed faults and post-merge maintenance. The Cursor longitudinal study and real-world technical-debt observations support narrower outcomes; commit-volume studies offer an *activity* comparison rather than direct evidence of architectural smells.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Generated duplication and missed reuse
nodes.summary: Examine why agents may create a new helper instead of reusing established abstractions, or reproduce code patterns that appear appropriate locally. Introduce repository-aware design checks and dependency search before editing.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Architectural fit in a living codebase
nodes.summary: Evaluate stable module boundaries, reuse, data ownership, error handling and compatibility for the running change. Contrast a narrowly passing test with good architectural placement; the architecture-smell and code-reuse studies give direct signals, while historical code ownership data inform stewardship rather than prove a particular refactoring is correct.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Post-merge evolution and maintenance burden
nodes.summary: Assess follow-up fixes, code smells, reverts and reviewer corrections after merge. Explain how task type, PR size and agent identity interact with observed quality metrics.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Tracing quality across agents and projects
nodes.summary: Compare code emitted by different agents only after normalizing task complexity and project context. Distinguish acceptance and maintenance outcomes from intrinsic model capability.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Authorship is not stewardship
nodes.summary: Distinguish generated-code provenance from responsibility to explain, maintain and recover a component. Historic ownership–quality studies provide measured background; the claim that AI invalidates traditional authorship metrics is a reasoned proposal that deserves empirical testing. Do not use newcomer-participation statistics as proof of the same effect.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Architecture fitness in the approval service
nodes.summary: Compare the duplicated-rule patch and the domain-policy-module alternative against checks for stable public APIs, invariants, error semantics, expected reuse and rollback cost. Explain the rationale for choosing one design; these are proposed engineering fitness criteria inferred from smell and reuse studies, not metrics with a universal safe threshold.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: Two attack surfaces, two threat models
nodes.summary: Distinguish vulnerabilities introduced into product code from attacks through the editor, shell, tool adapter or agent harness. Identify assets, trust boundaries, attacker-controlled text and possible effects.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Functional correctness is not security
nodes.summary: Demonstrate how a transaction approval service may function under normal inputs yet leak data, bypass authorization or permit a malformed operation. Make separate correctness and secure-behavior criteria explicit.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: What vulnerability studies actually measure
nodes.summary: Explain benchmark prompts, scanner detections, repository selection, language differences and matched-human controls. Avoid extrapolating a vulnerability percentage beyond the study's method and population.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Security-directed generation and remediation
nodes.summary: Compare unstructured requests for secure code against concrete feedback from scanners, taint analysis and vulnerability examples. Show why external localized findings can be more reliable than asking a model to reassure itself.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Dependency provenance and hallucinated packages
nodes.summary: Trace an assistant-recommended library from generated import to registry resolution, signature or source integrity, allowed versions and transitive dependencies. Distinguish generating a nonexistent name from an actual compromised dependency.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Prompt injection through repository and tools
nodes.summary: Show how README files, comments, issue text and tool output can smuggle instructions into an agent action chain. Teach the separation of untrusted data from authority-bearing instructions and enforce execution controls outside the model.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Harness configuration, skills and external services
nodes.summary: Inspect approval scopes, shell access, MCP servers, extension manifests, logging, network access and secret injection. Define a configuration baseline with least privilege and explicitly trusted tool identities.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: A secure agent execution profile
nodes.summary: Construct a sandboxed run with short-lived credentials, network restrictions, pinned tools, audit logs and explicit human grants for destructive operations. Present these as defensible engineering controls whose effectiveness still requires testing.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: Security evidence and release decision
nodes.summary: Connect threat model, relevant tests, findings, accepted exceptions and provenance to the change dossier. Require an accountable owner to accept residual security risk instead of allowing agent confidence or functional tests to do so.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: The oracle problem in AI-generated software
nodes.summary: Define correctness claims, expected outcomes and the difference between independent requirements and implementation-derived assumptions. Explain why more tests can improve confidence only if they challenge the right behavior.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: A hierarchy of evidence
nodes.summary: Arrange static checks, unit tests, contract tests, integration tests, security tests, property checks, end-to-end tests and production monitoring by what each can actually prove. Resist the temptation to equate passing tests with absence of defects.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Preventing bug-shaped test generation
nodes.summary: Explain how a model writing tests against buggy code may encode the implementation's mistake as the expected result. Require tests to originate from independent examples or invariants wherever possible.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Regression tests for existing and changed behavior
nodes.summary: Derive old/new behavior tests from explicit domain partitions, current production contracts, boundary cases, invalid input and concurrency. Contrast with agent-written tests whose expected values can be biased by buggy code; FlowGen coding-benchmark results are not evidence about real-world brownfield regression-suite effectiveness.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Properties and adversarial counterexamples
nodes.summary: Formulate invariants such as 'an unapproved transaction cannot be committed' or 'each approval yields one audit event'. Add property-based generation and fault injection, defining the test objective before prompting the agent.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Benchmark success versus merge readiness
nodes.summary: Compare benchmark scores, human-maintainer criteria and realistic integration tasks. A patch that passes the designated test set may still be unacceptable due to maintainability, unintended changes or repository-specific constraints.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Independent checkers and correlated error
nodes.summary: Compare deterministic analyzers, human checkers, and a distinct LLM reviewing generated code. Use software-focused cross-model review results together with broader correlated-error research, being careful that model diversity is not statistical independence and that non-code judge benchmarks do not directly quantify SWE defect rates.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Bounded repair versus independent acceptance
nodes.summary: Specify a bounded loop of diagnose, attempt, retest and evidence collection, followed by an external checker and human owner. A local pass is only review-ready; repeated rejection without a cited policy or changed evidence triggers adjudication instead of unbounded reruns. The exact budget and escalation policy is an author-proposed mechanism to pilot.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: The acceptance evidence dossier
nodes.summary: Produce a compact change dossier containing intent version, design record, exact diff, test provenance, security results, residual risks and open questions. Distinguish 'ready for review' from 'accepted for deployment'.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: Why review becomes the scarce resource
nodes.summary: Show how faster generation can increase PR arrival rate, review queues, maintainer load and unmerged work. Connect review economics to the earlier distinction between code production and delivered value.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: The influence of code complexity and provenance
nodes.summary: Examine controlled evidence on reviewer attention, code complexity and the AI label. Explain why spending more time scrutinizing AI code does not automatically imply better defect detection.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Human intervention in agent pull requests
nodes.summary: Describe where maintainers revise, guide, approve or reject agent-authored changes, noting task selection and PR size. Use real PR traces as descriptive evidence of workflow, not universal correctness rates.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: What AI reviewers catch—and miss
nodes.summary: Compare field experience of automated review tools with experimental evaluation of functional and architectural defect detection. Separate faster cycle time and fewer comments from the quality of the merged changes.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: False positives, verbosity and developer response
nodes.summary: Explain why irrelevant comments impose reading cost and reduce confidence. Design review output as short, testable claims tied to concrete lines, failures or intent deltas.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Self-review, cross-model review and shared blind spots
nodes.summary: Explore model self-preference, correlated errors, different reviewer model orderings and independent critical checks. Show when extra critics help and when they merely repeat assumptions.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Automation bias in software review
nodes.summary: Anchor trust calibration in code-review provenance and gaze studies; add the broader automation-bias literature as a boundary condition rather than a directly transferable measured rate. Teach seeded-defect reviewer exercises and explicit reasons to override AI recommendations, while marking their benefit as an evaluation hypothesis.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Risk-based review allocation
nodes.summary: Route trivial, reversible changes through high automation and high-impact changes through explicit human review. Define risk features such as touched subsystem, permission changes, behavioral novelty, uncertainty and blast radius.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: From comments to accountable acceptance
nodes.summary: Establish a review protocol: check intent adherence, challenge evidence, identify unexplained behavior, decide on fixes or escalation, and record who accepts remaining risk. Close the review by updating shared system knowledge.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Why comprehension dominates brownfield work
nodes.summary: Start from classic field studies of navigation, code reading and maintenance to explain how much of development involves reconstructing existing behavior. Use this foundation to interpret the promises and limits of retrieval assistants.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Mental models, rationale and cognitive load
nodes.summary: Explain how engineers infer architecture, data flow, exceptional behavior and design intention from imperfect artifacts. Contrast source syntax with the higher-level understanding needed to make safe changes.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Authorship, ownership and stewardship
nodes.summary: Review research on ownership concentration, knowledge transfer and defect associations. Explain why AI code generation breaks the inference that the person whose account produced a commit necessarily understands it.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Context assembly for an agent
nodes.summary: Define the minimal context package for a bounded task: affected APIs, dependent modules, domain rules, prior decisions, tests and trusted references. Discuss retrieval misses, irrelevant context and source hierarchy.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Different forms of persistent memory
nodes.summary: Separate working context, episodic execution traces, durable semantic knowledge, structured entity relations and authoritative decision records. Contrast promising research mechanisms with what has actually been evaluated.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Memory consistency, decay and invalidation
nodes.summary: Describe how facts become stale as branches merge, policy decisions change and owners depart. Propose versioned memory entries with evidence links, time scope, explicit invalidation triggers and a human-owned conflict resolution path.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: A typed graph for software-specific knowledge
nodes.summary: Model contracts, modules, test oracles, reviewers, owners, incidents and architecture decisions as versioned, typed links. AriGraph demonstrates one possible episodic–semantic agent memory representation outside software engineering, not an empirical proof that a software knowledge graph improves maintenance outcomes; historical turnover research motivates the need.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: Turnover, succession and long-term maintenance
nodes.summary: Examine the historic evidence on developer departure and succession costs. Design handover records around rationale, untested assumptions, failure modes and ownership of future modifications.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: A verified memory handoff
nodes.summary: Complete the running case by storing approved intent and design decisions with links to tests, diff and reviewers. Add an invalidation example when the jurisdiction rule changes, then ask a new engineer to explain the system unaided.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: Short-term task success versus retained understanding
nodes.summary: Distinguish task correctness during AI assistance from comprehension measured when assistance is removed. Prioritize developer learning experiments, compare beginner-code comprehension studies, and explicitly avoid transferring numeric effects from essay-writing EEG experiments to software programming.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Comprehension debt is distinct from technical debt
nodes.summary: Define a gap between code shipped and knowledge retained by the team. Ground the term in diary observations from student software projects, and contrast those qualitative patterns with controlled comprehension experiments; do not claim a quantified professional-team effect solely from student self-reports.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Novices, misconceptions and verification difficulty
nodes.summary: Show why beginners may accept code they cannot evaluate, produce changes that burden maintainers and struggle to detect violations of a natural-language request. Explain the risks without treating all novice use as harmful.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Cognitive offloading, physiology and limitations
nodes.summary: Separate the theoretical augmentation-trap hypothesis from biometric measurements made during AI-assisted coding and from essay-writing EEG results. Physiological activation is not a direct proxy for software correctness or durable learning; present testable hypotheses for the running case.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Learning through explanations, repairs and code tours
nodes.summary: Contrast model-only explanations with expert-curated tours, debugging exercises and tests built by the learner. Show how scaffolding can turn assistance into active learning instead of answer consumption.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Onboarding is a long process, not a first PR
nodes.summary: Use classic organizational studies to distinguish first edit, first independent task, file-level breadth and mastery of central components. Identify what an agent can accelerate and what requires social and architectural participation.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Mentoring and apprenticeship in a team with agents
nodes.summary: Propose explicit learning opportunities: requirements interviews, adversarial testing, reviewer rotation, post-incident explanations and teach-back sessions. Link the choices to the risk that automation removes entry-level tasks that once built expertise.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Measuring retention and engineering fluency
nodes.summary: Define assessments such as independent bug diagnosis, rationale recall, transfer to an unfamiliar module and maintenance after thirty days. Treat self-rated confidence and IDE activity as supplementary, not decisive, measures.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: A practical capability-development contract
nodes.summary: End with an onboarding plan for the approval subsystem: reading map, bounded agent use, one unassisted diagnosis, a supervised review and scheduled follow-up. Connect individual competence to team-level allocation of responsibility.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: From individual productivity to team throughput
nodes.summary: Discuss interfaces between feature engineers, reviewers, SRE, security, product and architecture. Model queueing effects when agent output accelerates faster than human validation capacity.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: New division of labor in engineering teams
nodes.summary: Distinguish intent owner, system steward, agent operator, verifier, reviewer, release authority and incident responder. Avoid treating these as necessarily new job titles; often they are explicit accountabilities within existing roles.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Policies that make expectations visible
nodes.summary: Compare permissive, restrictive and conditional open-source AI-use policies. Explain why disclosure, traceability, quality expectations and author responsibility may be more practical than blanket acceptance or blanket bans.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Executable policy as an engineering proposal
nodes.summary: Translate clear authority boundaries into checks for allowed tools, data handling, intent revision, test provenance, review thresholds and deployment permissions. Blueprint First/Model Second demonstrates constrained orchestration on a non-SWE tool benchmark; it supplies a design analogy rather than enterprise evidence for this policy stack.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: Agile team work with agent-produced increments
nodes.summary: Carry a late requirements change across backlog, versioned contract, independent tests and safe incremental release while several agents operate. Use observed agent-PR review and OSS policy practices to motivate coordination; explicitly resist inferring real-team agile throughput from FlowGen's code-generation benchmarks.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: Human accountability, conflicts and escalation
nodes.summary: Define who may authorize risky operations, interpret ambiguous requirements or accept an exception. Specify a path when the loop passes its checks but an orchestrator or reviewer disagrees, including reasons, limited retries and human arbitration.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: Maintainer load and newcomer participation
nodes.summary: Separate per-PR review burden, aggregate maintainer queues and newcomer participation effects rather than assuming that more complex generated changes automatically exclude newcomers. Combine qualitative slop observations with the causal newcomer-participation study, distinguishing its estimated association from a universal rule.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Knowledge handoff and stewardship rights
nodes.summary: Make ownership transfer operational: name current system stewards, define who can modify acceptance contracts, schedule knowledge refresh and attach verified design rationale to handover. This applies the turnover and succession evidence of Chapter 9 to a team policy decision, rather than repeating a literature review of code ownership.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Staged deployment gates, not a guaranteed ROI
nodes.summary: Build a rollout policy spanning sandbox pilots, low-risk changes and audited production use, with limits on review queues and rollback thresholds. DORA ROI is a practitioner planning framework and vendor/industry reports are contextual, not proof that a particular deployment stage yields a given return.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: Economics of the entire engineering loop
nodes.summary: Define the total cost of an accepted change: discovery, development, verification, review, tool consumption, infrastructure, integration, operations, remediation and learning. Distinguish cash costs, capacity costs and risk-weighted losses.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Why cheap generation may increase total cost
nodes.summary: Connect increased code and commit activity to reviewer queues, larger changes, incidents, complexity and delayed maintenance. Show the conditions under which local speed gains disappear from long-run economics.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Choosing the least-cost adequate level of autonomy
nodes.summary: Present a decision model comparing human-only, pair assistance, bounded agent and agent-plus-independent-checker. Define acceptance probabilities, verifier effort and uncertain loss as parameters to measure in a local pilot, not as empirically known constants obtained from conceptual position papers.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.label: Estimating return without fabricated certainty
nodes.summary: Teach incremental ROI, baselines, opportunity cost, treatment spillovers, observation periods and uncertainty intervals. Reserve scenario estimates for decision analysis and do not present assumed review costs as measured empirical facts.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Jobs, hiring, vacancy flows and unequal cohorts
nodes.summary: Keep employment stocks, hiring, vacancies, promotions and job postings distinct. Compare the version-specific Stanford early-career estimate, firm-level Copilot hiring evidence, and Norwegian administrative findings as outcomes drawn from different settings—not independent replications of the same causal effect.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Alternative causes of junior-market change
nodes.summary: Compare long-run vacancy timing, seniority-skewed job postings, remote mentorship and macroeconomic explanations before attributing junior outcomes to coding agents. Gallacher's Indeed article is descriptive trend analysis, *not* a randomized experiment, and chronology alone does not establish causality.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: The apprenticeship and long-term skill economy
nodes.summary: Connect organizational demand for experienced engineers with the risk that entry-level work is automated away. Model the future cost of losing training pathways rather than equating fewer junior tasks with efficiency.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: Distributional effects and quality of forecasts
nodes.summary: Compare country studies, firm-level spending/hiring outcomes, skeptical economy-wide assessments and executive expectations without equating their endpoints or controls. Separate observed employment patterns from modeled long-run responses and survey expectations; headline national trends cannot identify an AI-specific effect by themselves.
nodes.method_status: research discussion

nodes.label: A reversible, risk-adjusted adoption decision
nodes.summary: Integrate measured cost per accepted change, quality, security, review capacity, learning and operational risk into a decision memo with uncertainty bounds, named owners and a rollback plan. DORA supplies practitioner ROI structure and governance papers supply possible policies; the proposed combined threshold remains to be validated in a pilot.
nodes.method_status: engineering proposal

nodes.summary: Loop engineering means configuring a system that discovers work, dispatches agents, checks outputs, records progress and repeats rather than manually prompting each step. Osmani identifies five recurring primitives: automations/scheduling, isolated Git worktrees, reusable skills, plugins and connectors, and specialized subagents. A separate persistent memory or task board is the sixth requirement for continuity. He also warns about verification, comprehension debt and unpredictable token costs.

nodes.label: Adversarial Agent Pattern
nodes.original_attribution_passages: ["\\paragraph{Context.} A specification has been approved and an agent (or chain of agents) has begun executing it. The specification is the authoritative source of truth, but the act of execution---turning prose into code, tests, configurations---introduces interpretive freedom. Whoever does the building also has the strongest incentive to declare the work done.", "\\paragraph{Problem.} A single agent that both implements and verifies its own output is structurally biased toward declaring success. Self-verifying agents rationalise away gaps between the artifact and the spec, hallucinate the existence of behaviours they did not implement, and---most diagnostically---``just change the test'' when the code under construction cannot be made to pass. Kent Beck identifies this as the dominant LLM failure mode in test-first workflows: the model treats the test as another mutable artifact rather than as the contract the code must satisfy. Without an external check whose incentive is inverted, errors compound silently across phases.", "  \\node[pcin] (spec) {SPEC\\\\(source of truth)};", "\\paragraph{Consequences.} \\emph{Benefits.} Hallucinated completions are caught at the role boundary rather than after merge. The read-only sandbox makes ``just change the test'' architecturally impossible: the Verifier has no write privilege over the artifact under audit. Failure feedback is structured (spec~$\\to$~Coordinator) rather than ad hoc, which keeps the spec the single source of truth and prevents the Implementor and Verifier from negotiating their way to a passing build. The pattern composes cleanly with gate enforcement (Pattern~C1) because the Verifier's verdict is the natural input to Gate~3 (verification gate). \\emph{Trade-offs.} Inference cost roughly doubles per task because the Verifier re-reads the spec independently. Latency increases because verification cannot be parallelised with implementation without losing the inverted incentive (a Verifier that watches the Implementor work is no longer adversarial). Coordinator design becomes the highest-leverage decision: a weak Coordinator that decomposes badly will produce both bad implementations and irrelevant verifications."]

nodes.original_attribution_passages: ["%  Sources: Ralph Copilot's per-cycle documentation model.]", "\\paragraph{Solution.} Every autonomous cycle produces a structured \\textbf{evidence pack}\\,---\\,three artifacts at minimum, written to a per-cycle directory under \\code{.specify/evidence/}. The \\code{prompt.md} captures the exact input the agent received: the spec excerpt, the constitution sections, the prior artifacts, the task statement. The \\code{result.md} captures what the agent did: the diff, the test results, the tools invoked, the decisions made and their rationale. The \\code{verdict.md} captures the agent's self-assessment: did the cycle meet the acceptance criteria? Which evidence supports that claim? Which open questions remain? The pack is committed to the repository (it is part of the source of truth, not a transient log) and is linked from \\code{tasks.md} so the trail from item to cycle to evidence is one click."]

nodes.label: Escalation Protocol
nodes.original_attribution_passages: ["%  Sources: BMAD's explicit handoff protocol; AI-RPI's escalation model.]", "\\paragraph{A1 --- Constitution-Driven Development.} Enterprise SDD generates the constitution through the \\code{@constitution} agent during \\code{sdd init}; the output lives in \\code{.specify/memory/constitution.md} and is loaded by every agent's reading procedure. Update before the first feature, then amend explicitly through a dedicated PR with team sign-off; never edit the constitution as a side effect of a feature PR. Adapted from Spec Kit's constitutional governance and Karpathy's \\code{CLAUDE.md} discipline.", "\\paragraph{A2 --- Clarify Before Plan.} Enterprise SDD wires this into Phase~1.3: \\code{@clarification} runs after \\code{@requirement-analyst} and before Gate~1. The P1/P2/P3 tiering uses the same priority taxonomy as the runtime escalation protocol (Pattern~D4), so the team learns one vocabulary for ``how blocking is this?'' Adapted from Spec Kit's \\code{/clarify} template and the \\code{CLARIFY\\_BEFORE\\_PLAN} rule first articulated in GSD.", "\\paragraph{A3 --- Progressive Specification.} Enterprise SDD's \\code{sdd new --progressive} mode marks the spec with the progressive flag and requires every Gate~1 check to compare the current spec against the previous iteration\\,---\\,if no \\code{[NEEDS-CLARIFICATION]} markers were resolved, the gate fails. Use only on well-understood feature \\emph{types} (UI iterations, integration extensions); set an iteration budget (typically 3) and treat budget exhaustion as the trigger to elevate the feature back to standard pipeline. Adapted from Spec Loop Engine's iterative refinement model.", "\\paragraph{A4 --- Red-Team Specification.} Run \\code{sdd skill run red-team-spec <feature-id>} after the author has self-reviewed and before Gate~1 is requested. The skill's instruction explicitly forbids the agent from confirming what the spec does well; its only output is failure modes. Findings flow into the same gap-closure analysis (Pattern~A5) used for traceability. The pattern is one of three Enterprise~SDD mechanisms that implement the inverted-incentive principle from the Adversarial Agent Pattern (C5). Adapted from security red-teaming practice.", "\\paragraph{A5 --- Gap-Closure Analysis.} Run \\code{sdd analyze --gaps} on brownfield projects after \\code{sdd ingest} has imported the existing repository structure. Use the prioritised orphan list to drive a small allocation of each sprint to retroactive specification (typically 10--20\\,\\%); resist the temptation to declare a ``spec sprint'' that pauses feature delivery, which historically produces specs nobody references. Adapted from AI-RPI Protocol's traceability model.", "\\paragraph{B3 --- Anti-Sycophancy Enforcement.} Enterprise SDD ships the rule as part of the shared \\code{all-agents.instructions.md} so that every agent inherits the same wording; individual agents may extend the rule but cannot weaken it. The rule references the constitution, plan, and architecture pattern files explicitly, so the agent's challenges are anchored in artifacts rather than in vibes. Adapted from Karpathy's anti-sycophancy discipline and GSD's numbered rules.", "\\paragraph{B4 --- Convergence Review.} Enterprise SDD invokes convergence review through \\code{sdd gate check --convergence}, reserved for Gate~2 architectural decisions during autonomous execution. The two-model orchestration is wired into the autonomy policy so that budget accounting (Pattern~D3) accommodates the doubled cost. Adapted from the multi-model debate pattern in advanced LLM research.", "\\paragraph{D1 --- One-Item-Per-Cycle.} The boundary is enforced by \\code{autonomy-policy.instructions.md}: the policy contains a hard rule that no agent may begin a second item within a single cycle, regardless of remaining budget. Adapted from Ralph Copilot's one-item protocol and combined with Spec Loop Engine's per-cycle audit journal.", "\\paragraph{D2 --- Evidence-Pack Provenance.} Evidence packs are required in Autonomous-Governed mode and recommended in Autonomous-Guided mode; the autonomy policy refuses to mark a cycle complete without all three files present and structurally valid. Pair with the Adversarial Agent Pattern (C5): the Verifier's read-only audit produces its own contribution to the evidence pack, separate from the Implementor's, so the reviewer can see both perspectives. Adapted from Ralph Copilot's per-cycle documentation model.", "\\paragraph{D3 --- Budget-Gated Autonomy.} The default budget is set per mode in the autonomy policy; \\code{--autonomy-budget} overrides it on the CLI; \\code{sdd status --autonomy} reports remaining budget at any time during a run. Budget exhaustion produces the same handoff format as escalation (Pattern~D4) so the team has one vocabulary for ``the agent stopped, here is the state.'' Adapted from Spec Loop Engine's budget model and generalised from cycles to inference calls.", "\\paragraph{D4 --- Escalation Protocol.} Enterprise SDD encodes the three tiers in \\code{autonomy-policy.instructions.md}; escalation triggers (blocker, low-confidence, test failures, gate boundary) are listed in the policy with example classifications. Each cycle's evidence pack includes an \\textit{escalation log} with one entry per ambiguity encountered. Adapted from BMAD's explicit handoff protocol and AI-RPI's escalation model.", "\\item Each pattern was adapted from at least one public framework; knowing the origin helps in understanding the context in which the pattern is most effective", "\\item Patterns are not checklists; they are starting points for understanding a recurring problem and adapting the solution to your context"]

nodes.label: Research on developers' activity makes the distinction tangible. In their field study of professional developers, Xia and colleagues monitored work across seven
nodes.paragraph: Research on developers' activity makes the distinction tangible. In their field study of professional developers, Xia and colleagues monitored work across seven projects, 79 people, and 3,244 hours in the \emph{author-hosted manuscript}. The authors classified an average of 57.62\% of the observed time as program-comprehension activity. Their measurement deliberately extended beyond an IDE: the activities included searching or reading material in browsers and working with documentation. Table 7 of the accessible author manuscript breaks down where comprehension occurred, with average shares of 19.95\% for IDEs, 27.26\% for web browsers, and 10.38\% for document editors across the observed projects. These are categories derived from their observation and inference method, not a prescription for how engineers should schedule their days. \autocite{W170}

nodes.label: A smaller earlier study by Minelli, Mocci and Lanza examined fine-grained activity in the Pharo development environment. It recorded approximately 740 sessions
nodes.paragraph: A smaller earlier study by Minelli, Mocci and Lanza examined fine-grained activity in the Pharo development environment. It recorded approximately 740 sessions from 18 participants, totaling around 200 hours. Its Figure 3 assigns roughly 70\% of the instrumented activity to understanding, compared with about 5\% to editing. That result is sometimes repeated as if it describes every programming job. It does not. The sample mixed students and professionals, the IDE was specialized, and the authors inferred categories from interface events under explicit assumptions. The later, broader field study found a different percentage using a different observation frame. Both studies are useful precisely because they show that reading and reconstructing system behavior consume substantial attention while resisting a universal, context-free ratio. \autocite{W176}

nodes.label: As the scope expands, the engineer's role changes from selecting one suggestion at a time to supervising a sequence of decisions that may already have affected
nodes.paragraph: As the scope expands, the engineer's role changes from selecting one suggestion at a time to supervising a sequence of decisions that may already have affected the workspace. The distinction has empirical grounding, although the specific effects remain context-dependent. Chen and colleagues compared GitHub Copilot with OpenHands in a controlled user study involving 20 recruited students, many of whom reported some professional programming experience. Participants worked on both systems, with 40 minutes allocated to each condition, using tasks such as fixing repository issues, adding features and conducting research. The study design deliberately captured tool interactions and final code snapshots as different measurements. This provides a useful illustration of different human--tool workflows, but its small and selected population is not proof that one delegation level will always produce better enterprise software. \autocite{W002}

nodes.label: A very different kind of evidence comes from Liu and colleagues' characterization of GitHub Copilot production-scale traces. Their June 2026 sampled dataset cov
nodes.paragraph: A very different kind of evidence comes from Liu and colleagues' characterization of GitHub Copilot production-scale traces. Their June 2026 sampled dataset covered approximately 3.2 million users, 13 million agent sessions and 761 million model calls. At that scale, a user's instruction often begins a sequence of model inferences and tool executions. The paper's first table describes a workload whose machine-side steps can substantially outnumber the user's turns. These are observations about execution structure and inference infrastructure, not about how many resulting patches passed an independent engineering review. \autocite{W012}

nodes.label: Jeremy Osborn's essay in \emph{Communications of the ACM} offers a useful framing rather than an experimental estimate. In the portion independently available f
nodes.paragraph: Jeremy Osborn's essay in \emph{Communications of the ACM} offers a useful framing rather than an experimental estimate. In the portion independently available from ACM's official publication channel, he describes programming as increasingly dependent on reasoning and judgment when assistance reduces the burden of low-level recall. The argument has intuitive force: a developer who no longer writes a serializer manually still needs to decide whether its error handling, data contracts and security assumptions fit the system. It is an \textbf{opinion and synthesis}, however, not a measurement establishing how much time has moved from coding to review. The official text inspected for this chapter is unpaginated and partial; the exact journal-page reference remains an editorial action before publication. \autocite{W122}

nodes.label: Hoda's proposal for \emph{agentic software engineering beyond code} approaches the same development from a broader angle. Its whole-of-process diagram places hu
nodes.paragraph: Hoda's proposal for \emph{agentic software engineering beyond code} approaches the same development from a broader angle. Its whole-of-process diagram places human and agentic work across requirements, design, development, operations and ethical concerns. This is an explicit research vision, with preliminary principles and vocabulary, rather than evidence that an already deployed autonomous process performs the entire lifecycle reliably. The distinction matters. A vision can organize the questions engineering teams should ask without answering those questions empirically. \autocite{W153}

nodes.label: The research gives reasons to consider this structure, without establishing that these exact gates have been experimentally validated as a package. Farrag's 202
nodes.paragraph: The research gives reasons to consider this structure, without establishing that these exact gates have been experimentally validated as a package. Farrag's 2026 multivocal review combines 67 selected sources with a separately described \emph{illustrative} four-month exercise across three teams and 14 engineers (eight mid-level, six senior). The paper does not randomize teams or identify an external contemporaneous control group; its lead-time, hotfix and rollback ranges therefore cannot establish the causal efficacy of specification governance. Its proposed separation of specifications and checking remains a design input, not a calibrated performance claim. \autocite{W011}

nodes.label: Return to the request for configurable approval rules. An agent might have permission to create configuration fixtures, inspect code paths, run tests and prepar
nodes.paragraph: Return to the request for configurable approval rules. An agent might have permission to create configuration fixtures, inspect code paths, run tests and prepare a pull request. That permission does not establish the legal meaning of approval, the acceptable residual risk of a routing failure, or who is entitled to waive a failed check. Chen and colleagues' controlled comparison makes the interaction difference concrete, because the two tools induced different patterns of human participation. It did not test whether a coding agent should be allowed to accept financial policy changes. Hoda's whole-of-process vision similarly places agency on a continuum within human-controlled socio-technical work; it offers a conceptual map rather than a production authorization matrix. \autocite{W153,W002}

nodes.label: LaToza, Venolia and DeLine examined developers' work habits through two surveys and eleven interviews. They found that engineers often expended significant effo
nodes.paragraph: LaToza, Venolia and DeLine examined developers' work habits through two surveys and eleven interviews. They found that engineers often expended significant effort recovering implicit knowledge by exploring code or interrupting colleagues, while design documents failed to capture enough rationale for easy recovery. This was research from 2006, before current coding agents, yet the underlying constraint remains recognizable. Systems do not store all their meaningful requirements in a single file; much of the explanation for their shape is distributed among people, operational history and partial artifacts. \autocite{W186}

nodes.label: Xia and colleagues add a useful observational perspective: comprehension occurs across several tools, not only through source browsing. Web searches, documentat
nodes.paragraph: Xia and colleagues add a useful observational perspective: comprehension occurs across several tools, not only through source browsing. Web searches, documentation and communication are part of the activity being measured. An AI agent that reads the repository but cannot access, authenticate or interpret the relevant external context may build a coherent model of the code while missing the intended behavior. Conversely, giving it unrestricted access to external systems may expose secrets or permit actions beyond the task. Better context must be combined with bounded authority. \autocite{W170}

nodes.label: Cui and colleagues studied workplace rollout of a coding assistant and reported greater task output, operationalized in the inspected working manuscript through
nodes.paragraph: Cui and colleagues studied workplace rollout of a coding assistant and reported greater task output, operationalized in the inspected working manuscript through measures including pull requests. That endpoint is useful for studying the intervention, but does not directly measure delivered production capability. \autocite{W003}

nodes.label: Becker and colleagues instead timed experienced maintainers working on issues in repositories they knew well. Their early-2025 randomized comparison reported lo
nodes.paragraph: Becker and colleagues instead timed experienced maintainers working on issues in repositories they knew well. Their early-2025 randomized comparison reported longer completion time when AI was allowed. The difference from the workplace study begins with the work and measurement settings, not necessarily with a defective experiment. \autocite{W023}

nodes.label: Ownership research explains another part of the example's design. Greiler, Herzig and Czerwonka replicated work linking source ownership patterns to bug-pronene
nodes.paragraph: Ownership research explains another part of the example's design. Greiler, Herzig and Czerwonka replicated work linking source ownership patterns to bug-proneness, examining four Microsoft products. They found meaningful correlations between ownership measures and bug labels. That supports asking who knows and maintains the routing code; it does not prove that assigning a new owner or increasing ownership concentration would causally fix our fabricated defect. Likewise, Xia's comprehension study supports the need to inspect existing behavior, not a particular policy for financial transactions. The service and all its outputs are teaching artifacts, not observations made by those researchers. \autocite{W175,W170}

nodes.label: Demirer, Musolff and Yang examine tool adoption at several production endpoints and report that increases in coding activity attenuate at later stages. Their ve
nodes.paragraph: Demirer, Musolff and Yang examine tool adoption at several production endpoints and report that increases in coding activity attenuate at later stages. Their versioned observational analysis reinforces the need to distinguish commits, projects and releases; it does not establish a conversion factor between them. Chapter~\ref{chap:02} examines the estimates, while Appendix~\ref{app:methodology} records version and verification limits. \autocite{W010}

Ziegler and colleagues\textquotesingle{} work on neural code completion helps frame the local interaction: suggestion acceptance and perceived usefulness matter
nodes.paragraph: Ziegler and colleagues\textquotesingle{} work on neural code completion helps frame the local interaction: suggestion acceptance and perceived usefulness matter to the person at the keyboard, but are not interchangeable with system throughput. Demirer, Musolff and Yang explicitly separate commits, projects and releases. Their September 2026 NBER revision reports cumulative increases in commits of approximately 30\%, 180\% and 240\% across successive tool generations, while the last effect falls to about 80\% at the project level and 30\% at the release level. These are observational estimates for their sampled developers and tool periods, not conversion factors that can be imposed on an arbitrary team. \autocite{W009,W010}

nodes.label: Cui and colleagues report three field experiments involving 4,867 developers and a pooled increase of 26.08\% in completed tasks, with a reported standard error
nodes.paragraph: Cui and colleagues report three field experiments involving 4,867 developers and a pooled increase of 26.08\% in completed tasks, with a reported standard error of 10.3 percentage points, in the published Management Science abstract. The journal\textquotesingle s detailed tables still require parity checking against earlier manuscript versions, so we use the publisher-confirmed aggregate without inventing a table citation. \autocite{W003}

nodes.label: Paradis and colleagues randomized 96 Google engineers and estimated roughly 21\% less time spent on a particular complex task with AI assistance; the authors em
nodes.paragraph: Paradis and colleagues randomized 96 Google engineers and estimated roughly 21\% less time spent on a particular complex task with AI assistance; the authors emphasize that their interval is wide and that the result should not be generalized across tools and workflows. \autocite{W008}

nodes.label: Two experiments can disagree without one being defective. Becker and colleagues studied sixteen experienced open-source developers completing 246 tasks in repos
nodes.paragraph: Two experiments can disagree without one being defective. Becker and colleagues studied sixteen experienced open-source developers completing 246 tasks in repositories they knew well. In their early-2025 tool setting, allowing AI increased completion time by about 19\%. Developers had expected acceleration, and after participating still believed the tool had helped. Paradis and colleagues\textquotesingle{} Google trial instead estimated a roughly 21\% reduction in task time in its own environment. \autocite{W023,W008} Figure~\ref{fig:ch02-research-1} isolates the first study's disagreement: both subjective estimates fall below zero, meaning less task time, while the measured effect is above zero. Retrospective confidence therefore remains a different signal from timed performance.

nodes.label: Agarwal and colleagues examine code and maintenance signals associated with AI development tools; He and colleagues analyze the trade-off between short-term vel
nodes.paragraph: Agarwal and colleagues examine code and maintenance signals associated with AI development tools; He and colleagues analyze the trade-off between short-term velocity and longer-term quality in Cursor-associated development. These studies motivate a joint productivity-and-maintainability lens, but their particular measurements and causal identification should be verified against the exact source versions before their detailed coefficients are used. \autocite{W001,W004}

nodes.label: Software work moves through a chain of constraints. A developer can produce more patches than reviewers can evaluate, and a reviewer can approve more changes th
nodes.paragraph: Software work moves through a chain of constraints. A developer can produce more patches than reviewers can evaluate, and a reviewer can approve more changes than a release train can safely deploy. Queueing, dependency coordination and operational validation determine whether local speed becomes end-to-end delivery. The September NBER findings offer an unusually clear illustration: large changes in commits are accompanied by much smaller changes in releases. The authors interpret the attenuation through complementarity and production bottlenecks, but their fitted economic model is not a universal law of software organizations. \autocite{W010}

nodes.label: \noindent\textbf{The apparently finished patch.} Osmani calls attention to a ``70\% problem'' in AI-assisted development: a convincing prototype arrives quickly
nodes.paragraph: \noindent\textbf{The apparently finished patch.} Osmani calls attention to a ``70\% problem'' in AI-assisted development: a convincing prototype arrives quickly, while the difficult work of integrating it, handling exceptions and sustaining it in production remains \osmanicite{O049}. The percentage belongs to his practitioner shorthand; it is neither a universal completion rate nor a measured treatment effect. His separate review of productivity evidence also distinguishes personal speed from team delivery \osmanicite{O029}. The useful engineering question is therefore not how close the generated patch \emph{looks} to completion, but where its next unresolved gate sits.

nodes.label: Studies of Cursor-associated development and autonomous-agent maintenance raise this concern, but static-analysis warnings, cognitive complexity, defects, vulne
nodes.paragraph: Studies of Cursor-associated development and autonomous-agent maintenance raise this concern, but static-analysis warnings, cognitive complexity, defects, vulnerabilities and incidents are different outcomes. A warning count cannot be described as an observed exploit, and a complexity metric is not itself a measured future outage. We should keep these measures distinct and avoid combining them into a fabricated \textquotesingle quality score.\textquotesingle{} \autocite{W004,W054}

nodes.label: The early-2025 METR experiment is a useful warning because developers\textquotesingle{} forecasts and retrospective impressions diverged from the measured task-
nodes.paragraph: The early-2025 METR experiment is a useful warning because developers\textquotesingle{} forecasts and retrospective impressions diverged from the measured task-time effect. The May 2026 METR survey \autocite{W020} retained 349 responses after excluding 10 of 359 unique entries: participants reported median value multipliers across alternative questions of about 1.4--2 times, compared with approximately three times for perceived task speed. Email response rates were around two per cent and roughly 70\% of respondents received compensation, with convenience recruitment. The headline values are therefore \emph{self-reported counterfactual beliefs}, rather than tested throughput multipliers or evidence that 349 projects shipped more value. Later observations can inform hypotheses about tool familiarity, but retrospective perception is not observed elapsed time and neither can be silently treated as a randomized productivity effect. \autocite{W023,W020}

nodes.label: Pre-register task eligibility, assignment, tool versions, success criteria, exclusions, independent review and stopping conditions. Keep every assigned task, in
nodes.paragraph: Pre-register task eligibility, assignment, tool versions, success criteria, exclusions, independent review and stopping conditions. Keep every assigned task, including failures and abandonment. Orosz and Laura Tacho's account of company measurement practices combines delivery, quality and developer experience rather than relying on activity alone \oroszcite{P061}. For this pilot, turn that motivation into a measurement contract: each signal needs a unit, collection window and declared decision.

A code completion tool suggests text within a human-directed edit. An agentic coding system can read repository files, decide which files to inspect next, call
nodes.paragraph: A code completion tool suggests text within a human-directed edit. An agentic coding system can read repository files, decide which files to inspect next, call tools, apply patches and react to the resulting outputs. That greater delegation changes the system\textquotesingle s exposure to untrusted material. A README, dependency script or test output can influence the agent\textquotesingle s next action even though none has authority to issue operational instructions. Liu and colleagues\textquotesingle{} study of prompt injection in coding editors \autocite{W060} is directly relevant to that boundary, while their production-scale trace study \autocite{W012} provides a route for observing how tool-using systems actually behave. The precise attack rates and trace counts are not asserted here because their original result tables have not been verified in this draft.

nodes.label: Chen and colleagues\textquotesingle{} study of increasing automation \autocite{W002} examines how the distribution of developer activity changes as AI does more
nodes.paragraph: Chen and colleagues\textquotesingle{} study of increasing automation \autocite{W002} examines how the distribution of developer activity changes as AI does more of the work. Ehsani and colleagues\textquotesingle{} analysis of failed agentic pull requests \autocite{W191} focuses attention on observable failure outcomes. The two sources address different levels of analysis: a human workflow can feel more automated while a specific proposed patch remains unacceptable. We should not infer failure frequencies from the bibliography\textquotesingle s short annotations alone.

nodes.label: Pinna\textquotesingle s task-stratified study of coding-agent pull-request acceptance \autocite{W034} and Ehsani\textquotesingle s failed-PR analysis \autocite{
nodes.paragraph: Pinna\textquotesingle s task-stratified study of coding-agent pull-request acceptance \autocite{W034} and Ehsani\textquotesingle s failed-PR analysis \autocite{W191} are relevant to deciding which tasks warrant supervision. MirrorCode \autocite{W193} challenges simplistic assumptions that long calendar duration automatically makes a task impossible for AI, but its demonstrated capability does not supply a production reliability guarantee for arbitrary multi-week changes. Nor does a high success rate on selected benchmark tasks imply that an agent should control a high-consequence policy change.

nodes.label: \noindent\textbf{Two dimensions of delegation.} Osmani's practitioner framework separates \emph{agency}---how independently one agent can plan and act---from \e
nodes.paragraph: \noindent\textbf{Two dimensions of delegation.} Osmani's practitioner framework separates \emph{agency}---how independently one agent can plan and act---from \emph{orchestration}---how many agents can be coordinated, isolated and reconciled \osmanicite{O010}. His six illustrative levels describe a possible operating progression, not a validated organizational maturity scale. Keeping the axes separate makes the task-envelope rule more precise. One agent with permission to alter transaction eligibility has high-impact authority even in a single worktree. Several agents inspecting documentation in isolated, read-only workspaces can require more coordination without gaining authority to change policy.

nodes.label: Ehsani\textquotesingle s failed-PR study \autocite{W191}, Peralta\textquotesingle s analysis of why agentic pull requests are merged or rejected \autocite{W071}
nodes.paragraph: Ehsani\textquotesingle s failed-PR study \autocite{W191}, Peralta\textquotesingle s analysis of why agentic pull requests are merged or rejected \autocite{W071}, and Tie\textquotesingle s work on software-engineering pitfalls \autocite{W158} provide relevant research directions. In this chapter we do not attach invented proportions to those categories: their detailed coding schemes and tables must be checked in the source manuscripts first. The practical value is the failure taxonomy, which makes each rejection actionable.

nodes.label: Production trace research \autocite{W012} helps characterize actual tool-use patterns, and failed-PR research \autocite{W191} motivates explicit failure exits.
nodes.paragraph: Production trace research \autocite{W012} helps characterize actual tool-use patterns, and failed-PR research \autocite{W191} motivates explicit failure exits. Qiu\textquotesingle s blueprint-first deterministic workflow \autocite{W151} provides a cross-domain architectural analogy for separating policy from model execution; it is not direct evidence that this exact loop improves brownfield coding outcomes. The loop described here is an author-proposed method, and its effectiveness must be evaluated locally.

nodes.label: \noindent\textbf{What turns repeated prompting into an engineered loop?} Osmani identifies scheduling, isolated worktrees, reusable skills, connectors and speci
nodes.paragraph: \noindent\textbf{What turns repeated prompting into an engineered loop?} Osmani identifies scheduling, isolated worktrees, reusable skills, connectors and specialist subagents as common operational building blocks, and a durable external task or memory record as an additional continuity mechanism \osmanicite{O012}. His practical-loop discussion adds the need for a defined finish and risk-aware oversight \osmanicite{O006}. These mechanisms fit the state machine above only when the surrounding system assigns each a controlled responsibility:

nodes.label: \noindent\textbf{Keep the controls; question the extra machinery.} Orosz's public discussion of loop engineering asks whether custom coordination still earns it
nodes.paragraph: \noindent\textbf{Keep the controls; question the extra machinery.} Orosz's public discussion of loop engineering asks whether custom coordination still earns its complexity when existing tooling can supply some of the same mechanisms \oroszcite{P110}. This is a useful challenge to implementation choices, not evidence that the engineering responsibilities disappear. A human-led assistant, a bounded agent execution environment (a harness) and a custom coordinator can distribute those responsibilities differently. None is adequate merely because its name suggests autonomy or safety.

nodes.label: Hassan\textquotesingle s research roadmap \autocite{W152} discusses the architectural questions surrounding agentic software engineering, while Kim\textquotesin
nodes.paragraph: Hassan\textquotesingle s research roadmap \autocite{W152} discusses the architectural questions surrounding agentic software engineering, while Kim\textquotesingle s work on correlated model errors \autocite{W079} motivates caution about apparent consensus. These sources do not prove a general throughput gain from multi-agent development. The gain depends on decomposition, integration cost and the independence of verification.

nodes.label: Whitfill\textquotesingle s study of benchmark-passing yet unmergeable patches \autocite{W111} motivates the distinction between local pass and maintainer accept
nodes.paragraph: Whitfill\textquotesingle s study of benchmark-passing yet unmergeable patches \autocite{W111} motivates the distinction between local pass and maintainer acceptance. Purnachandra Reddy\textquotesingle s work on self-review failures in code modernization \autocite{W101} raises a related concern about trusting a model\textquotesingle s own explanation. The exact empirical rates remain outside this draft until the papers\textquotesingle{} result tables are verified. The governance rule we propose is operational: a checker or orchestrator must cite a concrete failing oracle, missing evidence or named policy before rejecting an otherwise green patch. After two repeated rejections without a traceable hook, autonomous retries stop and the case escalates to a named human.

nodes.label: Bhati\textquotesingle s lifecycle discussion \autocite{W095} and Farrag\textquotesingle s specification-driven governance proposal \autocite{W011} offer concept
nodes.paragraph: Bhati\textquotesingle s lifecycle discussion \autocite{W095} and Farrag\textquotesingle s specification-driven governance proposal \autocite{W011} offer conceptual ways to connect generation with reliability and cost. They should be read as proposed frameworks rather than controlled validation of the intent-first method used in this book. Lobentanzer\textquotesingle s expectation--realisation discussion \autocite{W013} supplies a contrasting warning about promises that outrun measured outcomes.
