Farrag\textquotesingle s specification-governance discussion \autocite{W011} and Hoda\textquotesingle s research on software work \autocite{W153} motivate disti
nodes.paragraph: Farrag\textquotesingle s specification-governance discussion \autocite{W011} and Hoda\textquotesingle s research on software work \autocite{W153} motivate distinguishing problem framing from implementation activity; Ehsani\textquotesingle s failed-agent PR study \autocite{W191} offers a relevant counterpoint about unsuccessful candidate changes. Their presence in the knowledge graph does not experimentally validate our phase separation. The proposed rule is narrower: authorize the external outcome at I1, then allow alternative designs at D0. Questions discovered later return to the intention authority instead of being answered by a model\textquotesingle s confident guess.

nodes.label: \noindent\textbf{Who owns a specification?} Osmani's advice on writing specifications for coding agents \osmanicite{O018} is useful for decomposition, explicit
nodes.paragraph: \noindent\textbf{Who owns a specification?} Osmani's advice on writing specifications for coding agents \osmanicite{O018} is useful for decomposition, explicit constraints and testable expectations. The warning is in the word \emph{truth}: a generated \texttt{SPEC.md} is a working proposal, not a policy decision. His separation of exploratory vibe coding and disciplined engineering similarly turns on which artifacts are reviewed and owned \osmanicite{O028}. In our running case three records have different authorship and authority:

nodes.label: The ledger should also record uncertainty. Suppose the existing service rounds monetary values before comparing thresholds. Is rounding a contractual rule or an
nodes.paragraph: The ledger should also record uncertainty. Suppose the existing service rounds monetary values before comparing thresholds. Is rounding a contractual rule or an implementation defect? The ledger marks it unresolved and assigns a decision owner. Chen\textquotesingle s and Hora\textquotesingle s work on team and organizational coordination \autocite{W150}, together with Hassan\textquotesingle s agentic engineering roadmap \autocite{W152}, provides useful context for authority and handoffs, but the particular JSON schema remains our proposal. The practical benefit of the ledger is that later reviewers can tell what was approved, what was assumed and what changed.

nodes.label: Drew Hoskins's discussion of diagnostics, excerpted and introduced in Orosz's publication, treats useful errors and warnings as part of the product experience \
nodes.paragraph: Drew Hoskins's discussion of diagnostics, excerpted and introduced in Orosz's publication, treats useful errors and warnings as part of the product experience \oroszcite{P082}. Apply that idea to the acceptance matrix: specify the recipient, stable condition, relevant policy revision, permitted next step and forbidden side effects of each response. A diagnostic describes the situation; it does not authorize a policy change.

nodes.label: The examples should not be generated solely by reading the implementation. Doing so risks turning a bug into an acceptance criterion. They must come from an app
nodes.paragraph: The examples should not be generated solely by reading the implementation. Doing so risks turning a bug into an acceptance criterion. They must come from an approved policy statement, with developers and test designers free to challenge missing boundary cases. Zhao\textquotesingle s verification research \autocite{W077} and related work on test quality \autocite{W097} motivate the importance of explicit external oracles, but the exact case matrix is author-created and synthetic.

nodes.label: A generated test can preserve the very defect it is meant to expose when its expected answer is inferred from the implementation. Zhao, Zhou and Cohen examine t
nodes.paragraph: A generated test can preserve the very defect it is meant to expose when its expected answer is inferred from the implementation. Zhao, Zhou and Cohen examine that failure mode using buggy and fixed program versions. Chapter~\ref{chap:07} develops the independent-oracle response and the study\textquotesingle s design limits. Here the implication is a contract rule: fix the intended behavior before using implementation output as test evidence. \autocite{W077}

nodes.label: Kaufman and colleagues provide a complementary human-review warning: in their experiment with 86 Python programmers, participants identified correct generated a
nodes.paragraph: Kaufman and colleagues provide a complementary human-review warning: in their experiment with 86 Python programmers, participants identified correct generated assertions with 74\% accuracy but incorrect assertions with only 49\% accuracy, while reporting similar confidence. This is evidence about judgment of assertions in that study, not a universal human-review failure rate. Together the papers motivate separating contract authorship, implementation and verification, then reviewing the test oracle itself. \autocite{W097}

nodes.label: The knowledge graph connects code-review and architecture research (\autocite{W099}, \autocite{W152}) with the engineering-structure literature \autocite{W148}.
nodes.paragraph: The knowledge graph connects code-review and architecture research (\autocite{W099}, \autocite{W152}) with the engineering-structure literature \autocite{W148}. These sources inform what to examine---diff scope, architectural drift and process assumptions---but do not authorize a design choice for this fictional service. If a proposed design reveals that the contract cannot be satisfied, the team raises a decision request at I1 or I2. It does not redefine success by making tests match the easiest implementation.

nodes.label: Hassan\textquotesingle s roadmap \autocite{W152} and research on rejected agent PRs \autocite{W071} motivate coordination and review without establishing an opt
nodes.paragraph: Hassan\textquotesingle s roadmap \autocite{W152} and research on rejected agent PRs \autocite{W071} motivate coordination and review without establishing an optimal gate sequence. Figure~\ref{fig:ch04-research-2} makes our proposed sequence explicit: validate the authorized delta before asking the model for a new patch, then rerun the affected contracts and independent checks. The dashed return brings unresolved evidence back to the control layer; it does not let the model silently rewrite intention. This keeps a late requirement small enough to trace without regenerating the entire system.

nodes.label: Qiu\textquotesingle s blueprint-first workflow \autocite{W151} provides an architectural analogy for constraining model execution, while Farrag\textquotesingle
nodes.paragraph: Qiu\textquotesingle s blueprint-first workflow \autocite{W151} provides an architectural analogy for constraining model execution, while Farrag\textquotesingle s specification governance \autocite{W011} motivates explicit checks. Neither source validates the exact intent-first state machine. The gate definitions are a normative engineering proposal, with observable exit conditions and named decision authority. The objective is to make the process inspectable while keeping change control lightweight enough for repeated increments.

Cotroneo and colleagues \autocite{W039} compare human and generated code across defect, vulnerability and complexity measures, while Improta and colleagues \aut
nodes.paragraph: Cotroneo and colleagues \autocite{W039} compare human and generated code across defect, vulnerability and complexity measures, while Improta and colleagues \autocite{W052} expand the comparison through paired function generation and language-specific analysis. The studies\textquotesingle{} abstracts describe different profiles of findings, not a single scalar score. In particular, \workposs{W039} ISSRE 2025 version of record studies more than 500,000 code samples in Python and Java. \workposs{W052} September 2026 preprint reports 787,562 function pairs spanning Python, Java and C. The latter generates candidate functions from human docstrings; that design provides a controlled comparison but does not reproduce every contextual constraint of an existing repository.

nodes.label: The unit of comparison becomes even more important once we look at the actual methods. Cynthia, Muttakin and Roy \autocite{W029} start with the AIDev curated su
nodes.paragraph: The unit of comparison becomes even more important once we look at the actual methods. Cynthia, Muttakin and Roy \autocite{W029} start with the AIDev curated subset of 33,596 agentic pull requests, select 8,106 bug-fix PRs, restrict them to 1,802 Python PRs in 206 projects, and finally analyze 1,210 that were merged. Their SonarQube procedure compares a base commit with its merged successor and records newly introduced static-analysis issues. This is a post-merge code-quality snapshot, not a longitudinal study of subsequent human repair or observed outages. The narrowing of the sample is part of the finding\textquotesingle s meaning: it does not describe rejected PRs, non-Python code, or all kinds of agentic work (\autocite{W029}, PDF pp.~1--2, Methodology and Table 1).

nodes.label: Kraishan \autocite{W054} asks a different question. The September 2026 preprint draws 37,623 labeled PRs from AIDev and a human comparison group in the same 2,8
nodes.paragraph: Kraishan \autocite{W054} asks a different question. The September 2026 preprint draws 37,623 labeled PRs from AIDev and a human comparison group in the same 2,807 repositories. It joins additional GitHub responses and follows a subset of 26,283 merged PRs for 90 days. Its maintenance proxies include changed-file follow-up activity and detected reverts; they do not identify every subsequent modification as a repair of an original defect. The paper explicitly acknowledges that the most-changed file is a proxy for whole-PR churn, revert detection can miss silent rewrites, and agents were not randomly assigned to tasks (\autocite{W054}, PDF pp.~2, 5, 7). These are different measurements, not rival answers to one identical experiment.

nodes.label: The apparent tension between \autocite{W039} and \autocite{W052} is instructive. \autocite{W039} reports that generated code is generally simpler and more repet
nodes.paragraph: The apparent tension between \autocite{W039} and \autocite{W052} is instructive. \autocite{W039} reports that generated code is generally simpler and more repetitive in its sampled Python and Java programs, alongside high-risk security findings. \autocite{W052} reports that AI functions can be shorter and less branching while displaying language-dependent security patterns; in its comparison, size-adjusted complexity carries less discriminating signal. Neither result implies that an AI-authored feature is automatically more maintainable than a human-authored one. Both rely on the precise definitions of a defect warning, a vulnerability category and a complexity statistic.

nodes.label: He and colleagues' Cursor adoption study \autocite{W004} uses observable committed configuration files to assign treatment, a proxy that may miss private or unc
nodes.paragraph: He and colleagues' Cursor adoption study \autocite{W004} uses observable committed configuration files to assign treatment, a proxy that may miss private or uncommitted adoption. Liu and colleagues \autocite{W055} examine technical debt in generated code. Agarwal and colleagues \autocite{W001} study later agent adoption in AIDev v3 repositories, stratified by prior IDE use. The W001 and W004 studies share investigators and related analytical techniques, and should be treated as related observational evidence rather than statistically independent validations; one study's percentage must not be substituted for the other's. \autocite{W001,W004}

nodes.label: An agent that sees only the function it is asked to modify may create a new helper rather than discover a reusable service already present elsewhere. The result
nodes.paragraph: An agent that sees only the function it is asked to modify may create a new helper rather than discover a reusable service already present elsewhere. The resulting patch can be locally sensible and globally redundant. Huang and colleagues \autocite{W031} report that AI-generated pull requests in their sample often overlook reuse opportunities, producing more redundancy even while reviewer sentiment may be neutral or positive. Wu\textquotesingle s clone research \autocite{W044} supplies a complementary topic, but its original manuscript has not yet been independently inspected for this chapter.

nodes.label: Zhu, Tsantalis and Rigby \autocite{W059} examine code and architecture smells in LLM- and agent-driven development. Their preprint describes structural degradat
nodes.paragraph: Zhu, Tsantalis and Rigby \autocite{W059} examine code and architecture smells in LLM- and agent-driven development. Their preprint describes structural degradation in the studied systems, but its strongest language about general laws should be treated as the authors\textquotesingle{} interpretation until the full methods and statistical results are inspected. Huang\textquotesingle s reuse findings \autocite{W031} provide a narrower observation. Historical ownership work such as Greiler \autocite{W175} helps frame responsibility and stewardship; it does not prove that a particular module layout is correct.

nodes.label: Kraishan\textquotesingle s churn analysis \autocite{W054} uses a proxy based on the most-changed file and normalizes by PR size. Its conclusion that none of the
nodes.paragraph: Kraishan\textquotesingle s churn analysis \autocite{W054} uses a proxy based on the most-changed file and normalizes by PR size. Its conclusion that none of the five agents imposes a measurably higher per-line maintenance burden in the observed window is therefore conditional on the measure, coverage, window and selection criteria. It does not contradict \workposs{W029} finding that merged bug-fix PRs can introduce static-analysis issues. Both observations can hold simultaneously. A code smell introduced at merge need not produce a later edit within ninety days, and later maintenance may arise for reasons unrelated to an original smell.

nodes.label: The studies discussed above follow different parts of maintenance. Cynthia and colleagues examine issues introduced by agent-generated changes, while Kraishan f
nodes.paragraph: The studies discussed above follow different parts of maintenance. Cynthia and colleagues examine issues introduced by agent-generated changes, while Kraishan follows subsequent file activity; Watanabe and colleagues study agentic pull requests more broadly. Their results require the version, denominator and follow-up window recorded in Appendix~\ref{app:methodology}. The targeted manuscript checks already performed do not amount to complete reanalysis of every source. \autocite{W029,W054,W036}

nodes.label: The studies\textquotesingle{} denominators also explain why apparently conflicting vendor stories should not be averaged. \autocite{W029} analyzes only merged P
nodes.paragraph: The studies\textquotesingle{} denominators also explain why apparently conflicting vendor stories should not be averaged. \autocite{W029} analyzes only merged Python bug-fix PRs and has no human baseline. \autocite{W054} includes multiple languages and a matched human comparison from the same repositories, then further narrows its longitudinal sample to PRs with a full 90-day observation window. \autocite{W036} follows 567 Claude Code PRs across 157 projects and reports that 83.8\% were merged, with 54.9\% of merged PRs integrated without further modification. Its manual task-purpose classification covers 213 agentic and 221 human PRs, with multiple labels allowed; it is not a randomized comparison of agent quality (\autocite{W036}, PDF pp.~1, 6--7).

nodes.label: AIDev underlies both \autocite{W029} and \autocite{W054}. Their overlapping provenance means that agreement between them should not be counted as independent re
nodes.paragraph: AIDev underlies both \autocite{W029} and \autocite{W054}. Their overlapping provenance means that agreement between them should not be counted as independent replication, even though they construct different subsets and measure different endpoints. A future synthesis could stratify by task type, language, patch size and repository, but the published aggregate tables alone are insufficient to perform that meta-analysis responsibly.

nodes.label: Kraishan\textquotesingle s cross-agent maintenance study \autocite{W054}, Pinna\textquotesingle s task-stratified acceptance analysis \autocite{W034}, and Mazlo
nodes.paragraph: Kraishan\textquotesingle s cross-agent maintenance study \autocite{W054}, Pinna\textquotesingle s task-stratified acceptance analysis \autocite{W034}, and Mazloomzadeh\textquotesingle s agentic-PR research \autocite{W057} point to the need for contextual comparisons. Their shared repositories or agent datasets must be checked before treating results as independent corroboration. A model\textquotesingle s capability score, an agent\textquotesingle s merge rate and the subsequent maintenance cost of its changes are different estimands.

nodes.label: Bird and colleagues \autocite{W182} examine associations between ownership and software quality in historical projects. Wheeler\textquotesingle s \textquotesing
nodes.paragraph: Bird and colleagues \autocite{W182} examine associations between ownership and software quality in historical projects. Wheeler\textquotesingle s \textquotesingle substrate collapse\textquotesingle{} argument \autocite{W189} challenges the continued validity of authorship-derived knowledge metrics under AI generation. These are different evidence classes: one is empirical background on ownership, while the other proposes a conceptual diagnosis of changing authorship signals. Xu\textquotesingle s newcomer-participation research \autocite{W058} is a useful boundary because participation and stewardship are not the same outcome.

Kapner et al.~\autocite{W053} study 3,171 public repositories: 2,660 assembled coding-agent setups and 511 skill collections. Their original PDF reports unpinne
nodes.paragraph: Kapner et al.~\autocite{W053} study 3,171 public repositories: 2,660 assembled coding-agent setups and 511 skill collections. Their original PDF reports unpinned MCP declarations in 9.8\% of setups, broad execution grants in 2.5\% and broad skill-tool preapproval in 3.8\%. The union of the three security-exposure categories affects 409 setups (15.4\%). These are configuration findings, not observed successful compromises. The authors explicitly state that runtime consequences and scanner recall remain unmeasured (\autocite{W053}, PDF pp.~1, 3--4, abstract, Table 1, §4). \autocite{W053}

nodes.label: Liu et al.\textquotesingle s Your AI, My Shell \autocite{W060} addresses runtime hijacking through poisoned development resources. Its original abstract describ
nodes.paragraph: Liu et al.\textquotesingle s Your AI, My Shell \autocite{W060} addresses runtime hijacking through poisoned development resources. Its original abstract describes 314 attack payloads covering 70 MITRE ATT\&CK techniques, with success reaching 84\% in studied editor configurations. This is a study-specific maximum, not a general attack probability; the large PDF remains pending page-level inspection. \autocite{W060}

nodes.label: Zhao et al.\textquotesingle s SUSVIBES study \autocite{W045} contains 186 security-sensitive feature tasks mined from real vulnerability-fix histories, covering
nodes.paragraph: Zhao et al.\textquotesingle s SUSVIBES study \autocite{W045} contains 186 security-sensitive feature tasks mined from real vulnerability-fix histories, covering 79 CWE categories. It evaluates functional and security tests separately. In the reported SWE-Agent/Claude 4 Sonnet setting, approximately 57\% of solutions pass functional tests, but only 11.8\% satisfy the security criterion; the authors report that 79.3\% of functionally correct solutions fail security checks. These percentages describe the selected benchmark and agent setting, not production incident rates (\autocite{W045}, PDF pp.~1--2, abstract and introduction; pp.~4--5, task verification). \autocite{W045}

nodes.label: \autocite{W041} offers a particularly important denominator caution. The authors\textquotesingle{} initial code-search results include documentation and other n
nodes.paragraph: \autocite{W041} offers a particularly important denominator caution. The authors\textquotesingle{} initial code-search results include documentation and other non-executable artifacts, and the later CodeQL sample focuses on selected languages. Even within the filtered sample, a file with no detected CWE finding is not thereby proven secure. Scanner coverage, query configuration and unsupported vulnerability classes all affect what can be found. Comparing this result with \workposs{W045} security-test pass rate would mix a file-level static-analysis endpoint with a task-level dynamic benchmark.

nodes.label: The strongest interpretation is therefore conditional: in \workposs{W041} explicitly attributed and filtered files, the selected scanner detected particular CWE
nodes.paragraph: The strongest interpretation is therefore conditional: in \workposs{W041} explicitly attributed and filtered files, the selected scanner detected particular CWE-mapped patterns; in \workposs{W045} selected feature tasks, agents frequently satisfied functionality without passing the security oracle. Both findings motivate independent checks, but neither supplies a universal vulnerability percentage for every AI-assisted commit.

nodes.label: Perry et al.~\autocite{W046} instead conduct a human-user experiment. Participants with AI assistance wrote less secure code on the studied tasks and expressed
nodes.paragraph: Perry et al.~\autocite{W046} instead conduct a human-user experiment. Participants with AI assistance wrote less secure code on the studied tasks and expressed greater confidence in their solutions. The result concerns a specific set of people, tasks and early tools; it is not directly comparable to the \autocite{W041} scanner counts (\autocite{W046}, PDF p.~1, abstract; detailed experiment requires version-specific checking). \autocite{W046}

nodes.label: Yan et al.~\autocite{W038} investigate security hints and explanation-guided repair in Python benchmarks. Their paper discusses an archive-extraction case in wh
nodes.paragraph: Yan et al.~\autocite{W038} investigate security hints and explanation-guided repair in Python benchmarks. Their paper discusses an archive-extraction case in which explaining the path-traversal mechanism guides a containment check for every archive member. The authors also acknowledge that benefits diminish when repairs are distributed or configuration-heavy, and that CodeQL cannot detect every dynamic vulnerability (\autocite{W038}, PDF pp.~26--28, case study and threats to validity). \autocite{W038}

nodes.label: Spracklen et al.~\autocite{W043} study package hallucinations across 16 models and 576,000 generated code samples in Python and JavaScript. Their original PDF r
nodes.paragraph: Spracklen et al.~\autocite{W043} study package hallucinations across 16 models and 576,000 generated code samples in Python and JavaScript. Their original PDF reports substantial differences across models and settings. These are generated package recommendations, not observations that every hallucinated name was registered or installed by an attacker (\autocite{W043}, PDF p.~1, abstract and subsequent methods). \autocite{W043}

nodes.label: \autocite{W060} shows the relevance of this problem for editors with shell and filesystem access. \autocite{W030} investigates workspace topology as an attack v
nodes.paragraph: \autocite{W060} shows the relevance of this problem for editors with shell and filesystem access. \autocite{W030} investigates workspace topology as an attack vector, while \autocite{W104} studies human detection of agent sabotage. The latter two papers remain pending full-text inspection, so no numerical effect is attributed to them here.

nodes.label: The \autocite{W053} authors\textquotesingle{} own scanner correction is a useful warning about automated policy checks. A rule may be syntactically precise yet
nodes.paragraph: The \autocite{W053} authors\textquotesingle{} own scanner correction is a useful warning about automated policy checks. A rule may be syntactically precise yet misunderstand the platform\textquotesingle s permission semantics. Before deploying a harness scanner as a hard gate, test it on allowed and denied examples, include known exceptions and record the scanner version. A green scanner report should mean that the configured checks passed, not that every possible configuration risk was excluded.

nodes.label: \autocite{W053} reports that 24.5\% of setups containing MCP configuration have an unpinned package declaration. The paper also describes a semantic mistake sha
nodes.paragraph: \autocite{W053} reports that 24.5\% of setups containing MCP configuration have an unpinned package declaration. The paper also describes a semantic mistake shared by the original scanner and its mechanical audit, emphasizing that configuration checks must be tested against the platform\textquotesingle s actual permission semantics (\autocite{W053}, PDF pp.~3--4, §4). These observations motivate reviewing harness declarations but do not measure how often the identified setups are exploited.

\caption{Untrusted repository instructions mus
Zhao, Zhou and Cohen \autocite{W077} study precisely this misguidance effect in generated unit tests. Their ISSTA 2026 paper uses paired buggy and fixed version
nodes.paragraph: Zhao, Zhou and Cohen \autocite{W077} study precisely this misguidance effect in generated unit tests. Their ISSTA 2026 paper uses paired buggy and fixed versions from Defects4J; the curated sample contains 318 focal methods covering 233 defects in 17 projects (PDF pp.~3--5, §2.2). Their definition is careful: a test that passes on buggy code is not automatically misguided, because many inputs behave identically in buggy and fixed versions. A genuinely misguided test asserts behavior that fails on the corrected reference (pp.~2--3). Their specification-based prompting reduces the problem in their evaluated setting, although a generated docstring is still an inferred specification, not a stakeholder authorization.

nodes.label: Kaufman and colleagues \autocite{W097} add a human-review warning. Their experiment involved 86 Python programmers who judged generated assertions. Accuracy was
nodes.paragraph: Kaufman and colleagues \autocite{W097} add a human-review warning. Their experiment involved 86 Python programmers who judged generated assertions. Accuracy was 74\% on correct assertions but 49\% on incorrect assertions, despite similar confidence (PDF p.~1, abstract). This does not mean all human reviewers perform at those rates. It means that human inspection, too, benefits from an independent behavioral reference. The book's proposed rule is to label each oracle with its authority and to keep maker-written tests supplementary to independently derived acceptance checks.

nodes.label: Whitfill and colleagues' METR study \autocite{W111} asks maintainers to judge SWE-bench-passing patches and finds that benchmark success does not guarantee merg
nodes.paragraph: Whitfill and colleagues' METR study \autocite{W111} asks maintainers to judge SWE-bench-passing patches and finds that benchmark success does not guarantee merge readiness. Its primary source is an online research note, so the audit cites named sections rather than fabricated page numbers. \autocite{W095} discusses lifecycle assurance as a proposed framework; \autocite{W080} concerns unit testing under LLM assistance. Their detailed methods remain to be inspected before numerical findings can be used.

nodes.label: \autocite{W077} compares test generation directly from code with a two-stage procedure that first derives a behavioral docstring and then generates tests from t
nodes.paragraph: \autocite{W077} compares test generation directly from code with a two-stage procedure that first derives a behavioral docstring and then generates tests from the docstring rather than the buggy body. The paper reports fewer misguided tests and more bug-finding tests under its experimental conditions (PDF pp.~2--4, 6--7). The authors' inferred docstring is not identical to our canonical intention contract: it can itself contain a mistaken assumption. In intent-first verification, the approved intention remains the authority, while inferred specifications are proposals requiring review.

nodes.label: \workposs{W101} work on self-review in code modernization motivates further caution, but its detailed numerical findings are not verified in this release. The p
nodes.paragraph: \workposs{W101} work on self-review in code modernization motivates further caution, but its detailed numerical findings are not verified in this release. The practical distinction is that the maker's self-tests and explanation belong in the evidence bundle while independent tests retain their own provenance and cannot be silently rewritten by the maker.

nodes.label: \workposs{W077} buggy/fixed comparison demonstrates the value of holding intended behavior constant across program versions. \workposs{W080} unit-testing resear
nodes.paragraph: \workposs{W077} buggy/fixed comparison demonstrates the value of holding intended behavior constant across program versions. \workposs{W080} unit-testing research and \workposs{W148} process-model benchmark work provide contrasting research directions, but neither is used here as proof that this exact brownfield workflow is optimal. The proposed procedure is iterative: late intention is versioned and traced rather than becoming an unrecorded prompt or triggering complete regeneration.

nodes.label: Finding a counterexample and reproducing its execution are different achievements. Orosz and Elin Nilsson's Antithesis report describes deterministic simulation
nodes.paragraph: Finding a counterexample and reproducing its execution are different achievements. Orosz and Elin Nilsson's Antithesis report describes deterministic simulation as a way to revisit the conditions behind a failure \oroszcite{P006}. The transferable lesson here is modest: retain enough state and ordering information to challenge the same behavior again.

nodes.label: \autocite{W045} and \autocite{W038} address vulnerabilities and secure code generation, which motivates negative cases but does not prove the completeness of ou
nodes.paragraph: \autocite{W045} and \autocite{W038} address vulnerabilities and secure code generation, which motivates negative cases but does not prove the completeness of our synthetic security checks. Detailed threat analysis belongs to Chapter 6. Here the engineering objective is to demonstrate that the independent oracle rejects representative wrong implementations, not merely that the intended implementation passes.

nodes.label: \autocite{W111} examines this gap directly by asking maintainers to evaluate SWE-bench-passing patches. The authors' METR report is a primary institutional rese
nodes.paragraph: \autocite{W111} examines this gap directly by asking maintainers to evaluate SWE-bench-passing patches. The authors' METR report is a primary institutional research note, not a paginated journal paper, and its review protocol should not be generalized to all repositories without qualification. \workposs{W192} AIDev data capture naturally occurring agent-authored pull requests; the W068 and W071 follow-on analyses reuse that shared corpus \autocite{W068,W071}. Their cohorts must not be counted as independently sampled replications. \workposs{W193} MirrorCode exercise instead concerns long-horizon capability. These sources measure different endpoints and cannot be pooled into one acceptance rate.

nodes.label: Independent verification can involve deterministic checks, humans, another language model or a combination. Independence does not follow automatically from usin
nodes.paragraph: Independent verification can involve deterministic checks, humans, another language model or a combination. Independence does not follow automatically from using a second model name. Two models can share the same faulty requirement, training bias or missing repository context. A human can also be misled by fluent but incorrect assertions, as \autocite{W097} illustrates.

nodes.label: Figure~\ref{fig:ch07-research-1} makes the conditioning in \autocite{W079} important: the bars compare how often two models choose the same wrong answer \emph{g
nodes.paragraph: Figure~\ref{fig:ch07-research-1} makes the conditioning in \autocite{W079} important: the bars compare how often two models choose the same wrong answer \emph{given that both are wrong}. They do not show how often the models fail overall. Agreement above the uniform wrong-choice baseline warns against treating consensus as independent evidence. Together with evaluator self-preference in broader LLM judgments \autocite{W082}, it motivates diversifying evidence sources; its quantitative transfer to software defect detection remains unverified.

nodes.label: Every attempt retains a task identifier, code hash, tool version, diff, tests, failure reason, time or cost budget and resulting state. \autocite{W101}, \autoci
nodes.paragraph: Every attempt retains a task identifier, code hash, tool version, diff, tests, failure reason, time or cost budget and resulting state. \autocite{W101}, \autocite{W095} and \autocite{W151} motivate caution about self-review and policy separation, but do not validate this exact retry policy. The steps in Figure~\ref{fig:ch07-research-2} represent distinct obligations: establish scope and contract, test behavior, review the evidence, and decide on release. Passing the test-oracle step does not satisfy the neighboring obligations. The staircase is a checklist of evidence boundaries, not a calibrated rise in reliability.

nodes.label: \autocite{W111} explains why benchmark success is insufficient for merge readiness. \workposs{W099} intent/drift research and \workposs{W150} study of repositor
nodes.paragraph: \autocite{W111} explains why benchmark success is insufficient for merge readiness. \workposs{W099} intent/drift research and \workposs{W150} study of repository AI policies provide context for review attention and organizational rules, but their full manuscripts still require final audit. The dossier format itself is the book's engineering proposal.

\includegraphics[width=\linewidth,height=.62\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/jpg/18_Figure_7_2_Architect.jpg}
\caption{Reliability grows through an evidence
The difference between code activity and delivery, introduced through Demirer and colleagues \autocite{W010}, explains why local coding gains need not become re
nodes.paragraph: The difference between code activity and delivery, introduced through Demirer and colleagues \autocite{W010}, explains why local coding gains need not become release gains. Research on review effort and AI-generated changes (\autocite{W063}, \autocite{W094}) addresses a different part of that chain: reviewers must reconstruct intention, understand a diff and assess the strength of its checks. A study measuring the number of comments cannot by itself measure whether those comments prevented defects. Nor does faster review imply a better decision if reviewers overlook the very risks that justify review.

nodes.label: Khojah et al.~\autocite{W069} use eye tracking and interviews in a Wizard-of-Oz review experiment. Their primary abstract reports that LLM provenance labeling i
nodes.paragraph: Khojah et al.~\autocite{W069} use eye tracking and interviews in a Wizard-of-Oz review experiment. Their primary abstract reports that LLM provenance labeling increased fixation time without changing the measured thoroughness of review. This observation cautions against equating attention, elapsed time, trust or accuracy. Its full participant-level methods and effect estimates still need examination before stronger numerical claims can be made.

nodes.label: Studies of review complexity \autocite{W073}, developer perceptions \autocite{W069} and review outcomes \autocite{W088} motivate separating patch size from cogn
nodes.paragraph: Studies of review complexity \autocite{W073}, developer perceptions \autocite{W069} and review outcomes \autocite{W088} motivate separating patch size from cognitive difficulty. Their detailed coefficients remain subject to original manuscript verification. The engineering point is that provenance is a clue about how a change was produced, not a verdict about its correctness. A human-authored patch can be unsafe, and a generated patch can be excellent; both need evidence appropriate to the affected system.

nodes.label: The review-trace denominator is particularly important. Duma et al.~\autocite{W065} report that 61.38\% of 33,596 agent-authored PRs have no recorded review, an
nodes.paragraph: The review-trace denominator is particularly important. Duma et al.~\autocite{W065} report that 61.38\% of 33,596 agent-authored PRs have no recorded review, and 84.0\% have no recorded review or only agent review. This is not proof that no human inspected the code: unrecorded discussion, local inspection and repository policy can escape the dataset. The same-repository comparison in the source bibliography also gives a much smaller contrast between agent- and human-authored PRs than a headline 84\% figure might suggest. AIDev-derived studies share underlying PR records, so repeated analysis is not independent replication. The full manuscript and sampling procedure must be checked before quoting adjusted comparisons.

nodes.label: A concrete production deployment and a benchmark answer different questions. Tantithamthavorn et al.~\autocite{W074} describe an Atlassian RovoDev reviewer depl
nodes.paragraph: A concrete production deployment and a benchmark answer different questions. Tantithamthavorn et al.~\autocite{W074} describe an Atlassian RovoDev reviewer deployment. Their original abstract reports 38.70\% of AI comments followed by code changes, approximately 30.8\% lower PR cycle time, and 35.6\% fewer human-written comments in their evaluated setting. The figures concern review workflow and follow-up action; they are not a measured reduction in escaped defects, and observational deployment confounders remain relevant. Zeng et al.~\autocite{W076} introduce SWRBench with 1,000 manually verified GitHub PRs and project context; benchmark precision and recall measure correspondence with selected ground-truth review issues, not the causal effect of deployment. The original abstracts support this contrast, while exact table cells and publisher pagination still require inspection.

nodes.label: AI review tools can identify suspicious patterns, propose missing tests and summarize complex diffs. They can also miss defects or invent problems that are not
nodes.paragraph: AI review tools can identify suspicious patterns, propose missing tests and summarize complex diffs. They can also miss defects or invent problems that are not present. Evaluations of automated code review (\autocite{W074}, \autocite{W106}) and related research \autocite{W081} investigate different aspects of that performance. A benchmark may count detected defects, while a field deployment may count developer reactions or review latency. These endpoints should not be combined into a single accuracy claim.

nodes.label: Research on review comment quality and developer response (\autocite{W064}, \autocite{W098}, \autocite{W096}) motivates measuring precision, actionability and r
nodes.paragraph: Research on review comment quality and developer response (\autocite{W064}, \autocite{W098}, \autocite{W096}) motivates measuring precision, actionability and review burden separately. The exact empirical rates remain provisional until the original papers are inspected. For the service, a warning that \textquotesingle the policy code may be unsafe\textquotesingle{} is not actionable. A warning that \textquotesingle the adapter retains the v1 €5,000 ceiling while INT-002 requires €3,000 for new requests\textquotesingle{} names an observable mismatch and supplies a path to reproduce it.

nodes.label: Orosz's publicly visible account describes teams reviewing AI-generated comments and routing changes according to their consequences \oroszcite{P118}. That crea
nodes.paragraph: Orosz's publicly visible account describes teams reviewing AI-generated comments and routing changes according to their consequences \oroszcite{P118}. That creates a further distinction: a human can validate every reported finding without establishing evidence for every material acceptance obligation. A quiet or filtered reviewer is not a coverage certificate.

nodes.label: Xiang et al.~\autocite{W102} give a particularly useful verification-cost counterexample. On 116 complete-case LiveCodeBench problems, review by Claude changes
nodes.paragraph: Xiang et al.~\autocite{W102} give a particularly useful verification-cost counterexample. On 116 complete-case LiveCodeBench problems, review by Claude changes Codex passing outputs from 83 to 104 (+21), at \$0.443 versus \$0.190 per task; the opposite reviewer ordering lowers Claude's successes from 106 to 96 while increasing modeled inference cost from \$0.226 to \$0.382 per task. Table~2 provides numerator and denominator for independent \emph{percentage arithmetic}, and Table~4 provides discordances for exact McNemar test rechecks. Neither calculation replays the model calls, proves transfer to repository review, or guarantees a cost-effective production policy. A reviewer remains accountable for independent oracles, acceptance and regression risk. Figure~\ref{fig:ch08-research-1} decomposes those net changes into failures fixed and previously passing answers broken. Read each two-letter label as writer then reviewer: the green and red bars must be considered together. More corrections can coexist with regressions, so a review policy needs both counts rather than a tally of helpful comments.

nodes.label: Other work on model self-review \autocite{W109} and correlated errors \autocite{W079} reinforces the need to examine the independence of evidence rather than co
nodes.paragraph: Other work on model self-review \autocite{W109} and correlated errors \autocite{W079} reinforces the need to examine the independence of evidence rather than count agreeing opinions. In the approval service, the decisive checker is a deterministic test derived from the authorized contract. A second model may inspect the diff and suggest additional counterexamples, but agreement between two models cannot override the high-risk invariant or the replay requirement. The review design should diversify information sources before it diversifies model names.

nodes.label: Studies of human interaction with AI review recommendations (\autocite{W083}, \autocite{W088}, \autocite{W091}) explore this question in different settings. The
nodes.paragraph: Studies of human interaction with AI review recommendations (\autocite{W083}, \autocite{W088}, \autocite{W091}) explore this question in different settings. The current draft does not assign them numerical effects without manuscript-level checks. A reviewer may be influenced by a confident explanation, a green badge or an apparently precise severity score. None of those cues establishes that the finding is correct.

nodes.label: Research on review allocation \autocite{W093}, intent-aware code critique \autocite{W099} and review quality \autocite{W104} supplies relevant context. The chap
nodes.paragraph: Research on review allocation \autocite{W093}, intent-aware code critique \autocite{W099} and review quality \autocite{W104} supplies relevant context. The chapter\textquotesingle s proposed decision table routes low-risk, well-tested changes to streamlined review; policy-sensitive or security-relevant changes require specialized reviewers and explicit acceptance evidence. A patch with missing intention authority cannot become low-risk simply because it is small.

nodes.label: \noindent\textbf{When ``read the draft'' meets review capacity.} In 2025 Osmani urged engineers to read AI-generated code as a draft, reasoning that inspection
nodes.paragraph: \noindent\textbf{When ``read the draft'' meets review capacity.} In 2025 Osmani urged engineers to read AI-generated code as a draft, reasoning that inspection preserves understanding and prevents plausible mistakes from entering production \osmanicite{O023}. His September 2026 essay \emph{The Code Nobody Reads} instead explores a future where exhaustive line-by-line human reading cannot scale and lower-risk changes pass through stronger automated checks \osmanicite{O001}. The two positions expose a real design question, not a blanket rule to abolish review: what assurance must be retained when human attention becomes selective?

nodes.label: Research on review outcomes \autocite{W107} and maintainer rejection of benchmark-passing patches \autocite{W111} motivates separating technical plausibility fr
nodes.paragraph: Research on review outcomes \autocite{W107} and maintainer rejection of benchmark-passing patches \autocite{W111} motivates separating technical plausibility from integration acceptance. \autocite{W105} provides a contrasting view of review tooling, but its detailed findings remain pending verification. The approval-service dossier includes the INT-001 and INT-002 contracts, the architecture decision, the patch hash, independent test results, the reviewer\textquotesingle s disposition of findings and an explicit acceptance field. Because the laboratory has no real policy-owner signature, its final state remains \textquotesingle ready for review\textquotesingle, not production accepted.

nodes.paragraph: \noindent\textbf{A brownfield permission map.} Osmani proposes green, yellow and red zones for mature repositories, assigned by people according to coverage, isolation, institutional knowledge and potential consequences \osmanicite{O002}. The labels are useful as a provisional routing shorthand, not a numerical prediction of defect probability:

nodes.label: Engineers maintain mental models of responsibilities, data flow, exceptional behavior and design rationale. LaToza, Venolia and DeLine\textquotesingle s explora
nodes.paragraph: Engineers maintain mental models of responsibilities, data flow, exceptional behavior and design rationale. LaToza, Venolia and DeLine\textquotesingle s exploratory surveys and interviews describe the effort involved in recovering that knowledge within one corporation. Their self-selected observations motivate a design problem, rather than establish an effect of AI-mediated memory. \autocite{W186}

nodes.label: Ownership research uses contribution patterns as proxies for expertise and relates them to quality outcomes. Bird and colleagues found such associations in two
nodes.paragraph: Ownership research uses contribution patterns as proxies for expertise and relates them to quality outcomes. Bird and colleagues found such associations in two Microsoft products; the study does not prove that changing ownership causally reduces defects. Wheeler\textquotesingle s argument that AI weakens authorship-based proxies is a separate conceptual claim. Together they invite scrutiny of the proxy, rather than a presumption that generated code is defective. \autocite{W182,W189}

nodes.label: A coding agent sees only the context it retrieves. Source files can be current while design notes are stale; tests may encode defects; summaries may omit author
nodes.paragraph: A coding agent sees only the context it retrieves. Source files can be current while design notes are stale; tests may encode defects; summaries may omit authorization. The studies of contextual and conceptual pitfalls mapped to W155 and W158 motivate careful selection, without establishing a universal context recipe. More retrieved material is not necessarily more useful evidence. \autocite{W155,W158}

nodes.label: An agent trace showing that nineteen tests passed is an episodic fact. It cannot prove that those tests cover the correct intention. A semantic card saying \tex
nodes.paragraph: An agent trace showing that nineteen tests passed is an episodic fact. It cannot prove that those tests cover the correct intention. A semantic card saying \textquotesingle Treasury ceiling €3,000\textquotesingle{} is incomplete without its effective policy version. An intention contract has stronger authority about desired behavior, but it may not describe every implementation dependency. The memory mechanisms mapped to \autocite{W157}, \autocite{W159} and \autocite{W160} explore different representations and retrieval methods. \autocite{W157} is ClawVM, published at EuroMLSys 2026, DOI 10.1145/3805621.3807648, pp.~1--12, rather than merely an undated bibliography entry. It proposes harness-managed typed memory pages and validated writeback; its evaluation includes synthetic workloads, twelve real-session traces and adversarial tests. Those results concern state preservation under the authors\textquotesingle{} fault model, not demonstrated improvements in a software maintainer\textquotesingle s understanding. The empirical transfer of these mechanisms to brownfield comprehension remains to be established.

nodes.label: We therefore propose explicit memory states: CURRENT, SUPERSEDED, STALE\_BY\_INTENT\_DELTA, DISPUTED and UNKNOWN. Each record includes source, revision, validit
nodes.paragraph: We therefore propose explicit memory states: CURRENT, SUPERSEDED, STALE\_BY\_INTENT\_DELTA, DISPUTED and UNKNOWN. Each record includes source, revision, validity scope, invalidation triggers and an accountable owner. These states are methodological proposals, not terminology empirically validated by \autocite{W157} or \autocite{W168}.

nodes.label: \noindent\textbf{Renew context before reusing it.} Osmani treats context as an engineered selection of repository facts and constraints \osmanicite{O031}, shows
nodes.paragraph: \noindent\textbf{Renew context before reusing it.} Osmani treats context as an engineered selection of repository facts and constraints \osmanicite{O031}, shows why long-running agents need durable handoff checkpoints \osmanicite{O013}, and recommends periodic audits of agent instruction files \osmanicite{O004}. Their practical synthesis for the approval service is a short renewal protocol. Before a new run, identify the context file's \emph{owner}, cite the source for each non-obvious invariant, record its \emph{intent revision and validity scope}, declare an \emph{expiry or invalidation trigger}, and keep procedural hints separate from tool permissions. Delete redundant instructions, quarantine retrieved text as data, and restart with an independently refreshed acceptance bundle when a material premise changes.

nodes.label: Anokhin and colleagues\textquotesingle{} AriGraph combines semantic relations and episodic observations for agents. Its evaluated environments differ from softw
nodes.paragraph: Anokhin and colleagues\textquotesingle{} AriGraph combines semantic relations and episodic observations for agents. Its evaluated environments differ from software maintenance, so it offers a representation mechanism rather than direct validation of this chapter\textquotesingle s handoff design. The IJCAI version and inspected locations are recorded in Appendix~\ref{app:methodology}. Our software graph still requires task-specific evaluation. \autocite{W160}

nodes.label: Turnover exposes missing rationale: a repository may build while a successor cannot explain an exception or assess its removal. Mockus\textquotesingle{} histori
nodes.paragraph: Turnover exposes missing rationale: a repository may build while a successor cannot explain an exception or assess its removal. Mockus\textquotesingle{} historical succession study and Rigby and colleagues\textquotesingle{} file-based knowledge-loss analysis examine aspects of this problem. Their observational associations and repository-derived proxies do not estimate AI-assisted handover benefits. Appendix~\ref{app:methodology} preserves their distinct samples, numerical checks and remaining limitations. \autocite{W185,W173}

Shen and Tamkin's main randomized study enrolled 52 Python-experienced participants unfamiliar with Trio, 26 per condition. After two tasks and up to 35 minutes
nodes.paragraph: Shen and Tamkin's main randomized study enrolled 52 Python-experienced participants unfamiliar with Trio, 26 per condition. After two tasks and up to 35 minutes of work, participants completed an unaided 14-question assessment. The authors report lower immediate comprehension with AI assistance (Cohen's $d=0.738$, $p=0.010$), without a statistically significant average improvement in task time. This is an immediate assessment, not a week- or month-later retention result. The source's percentage summary has an unresolved normalization inconsistency, recorded in Appendix~\ref{app:methodology}, \S\ref{app:commentary-ch10}; the chapter does not turn it into a precise loss-of-skill rate. \autocite{W118}

nodes.label: Ahmad's qualitative study analyzed 621 reflective diaries from 207 students over eight weeks. It describes black-box acceptance, context mismatch, dependency-in
nodes.paragraph: Ahmad's qualitative study analyzed 621 reflective diaries from 207 students over eight weeks. It describes black-box acceptance, context mismatch, dependency-induced atrophy and verification bypass, alongside a contrasting use of AI as a comprehension scaffold. These are recurring experiences in an undergraduate project, not an eight-week controlled retention test or measured industrial defect rates. \autocite{W154}

nodes.label: Anderson and colleagues examine changes to unfamiliar code using architecture sketches and explanations as well as task completion. That small study motivates a
nodes.paragraph: Anderson and colleagues examine changes to unfamiliar code using architecture sketches and explanations as well as task completion. That small study motivates assessing the mental model behind a patch; it does not establish its future maintenance consequences. The source's method and verification boundaries remain in Appendix~B. \autocite{W155}

nodes.label: Zi and colleagues studied 32 introductory-programming students across 160 task instances. The reported 32.5\% success rate concerns their generated-code \emph{c
nodes.paragraph: Zi and colleagues studied 32 introductory-programming students across 160 task instances. The reported 32.5\% success rate concerns their generated-code \emph{comprehension task}; it is not a defect rate in generated programs. The authors describe difficulties involving Python familiarity, language comprehension and automation bias. The population and tasks limit transfer to experienced maintainers. \autocite{W113}

nodes.label: Related work on novice contributions and attention to security motivates reviewing generated assertions before delegating cross-module changes; their uncomplete
nodes.paragraph: Related work on novice contributions and attention to security motivates reviewing generated assertions before delegating cross-module changes; their uncompleted primary-method audits do not justify numerical learning claims here. \autocite{W112,W067} Increase delegated responsibility with demonstrated judgment rather than job title or prompt count.

nodes.label: Lower perceived effort, eye-fixation measures or physiological signals are not interchangeable with later unaided performance. The biometric and offloading sour
nodes.paragraph: Lower perceived effort, eye-fixation measures or physiological signals are not interchangeable with later unaided performance. The biometric and offloading sources in the catalogue do not yet support a fully audited physiological effect here. \autocite{W116,W117} Work on essay writing is an adjacent comparison, not direct evidence of coding-skill loss. \autocite{W121}

nodes.label: Kara and colleagues' LACY system combines expert-curated tours with AI-generated explanations. Its industry co-design involved a legacy finance system exceeding
nodes.paragraph: Kara and colleagues' LACY system combines expert-curated tours with AI-generated explanations. Its industry co-design involved a legacy finance system exceeding 30,000 lines; reported quiz scores were 83\% for expert-guided tours and 57\% for AI-only tours. This is an immediate study outcome, not demonstrated retention months later. The intervention combines generation, curation and a reusable code-anchored narrative, rather than merely comparing the presence or absence of AI. \autocite{W156}

nodes.label: Onboarding also has social and procedural dimensions. Ju and colleagues' Microsoft study combines interviews with newly assigned developers and managers with fo
nodes.paragraph: Onboarding also has social and procedural dimensions. Ju and colleagues' Microsoft study combines interviews with newly assigned developers and managers with follow-up surveys. Its exploratory mixed-method design motivates attention to ownership and access to help; it does not identify an AI-mentoring treatment effect. \autocite{W163}

nodes.label: Historical work on developer fluency, ramp-up and distributed development motivates a staged view, not a universal time-to-productivity curve. Its remaining pri
nodes.paragraph: Historical work on developer fluency, ramp-up and distributed development motivates a staged view, not a universal time-to-productivity curve. Its remaining primary-source checks are recorded in Appendix~B. \autocite{W184,W178,W187} A local progression moves from explaining current behavior to repairing a bounded defect, reviewing another candidate, introducing a versioned rule and diagnosing an unseen failure. Each step provides a different opportunity to observe independent judgment.

nodes.label: Routine tasks can be both production work and occasions for supervised practice. Removing them changes the opportunities through which novices become independen
nodes.paragraph: Routine tasks can be both production work and occasions for supervised practice. Removing them changes the opportunities through which novices become independent, even when immediate output improves. The apprenticeship model offers a theoretical way to frame that trade-off; Chapter~\ref{chap:12} examines its economic assumptions. It does not establish a staffing rule or forecast this team\textquotesingle s skill supply. \autocite{W119}

nodes.label: \autocite{W162} maps the designs of 95 code-comprehension experiments published from 1979 to 2019: the corpus predates present-day agentic coding and is a syste
nodes.paragraph: \autocite{W162} maps the designs of 95 code-comprehension experiments published from 1979 to 2019: the corpus predates present-day agentic coding and is a systematic mapping, not a controlled benchmark of coding agents. Its ACM Computing Surveys version of record is volume~56, issue~4 (2024), article~106. A \emph{September 2026 corrigendum} \autocite{W162Corrigendum2026} documents a misordering that caused primary-study identifiers S1--S95 in the article and tables to disagree with the study reference list and replication package; a reanalysis must use the corrected mapping. \autocite{W170} observes professional activity but is not an intervention study. \autocite{W114} explores physiological correlates; its original full text still needs inspection, and those signals cannot substitute for demonstrated reasoning.

nodes.label: Corrigendum: 40 Years of Designing Code Comprehension Experiments: A Systematic Mapping Study
\noindent\textbf{Keep the reasoning repetitions.} Osmani's account of skill decay \osmanicite{O003} argues that fast autonomous implementation can displace the
nodes.paragraph: \noindent\textbf{Keep the reasoning repetitions.} Osmani's account of skill decay \osmanicite{O003} argues that fast autonomous implementation can displace the practice through which developers learn to predict, debug and explain systems. His ``80\% problem'' \osmanicite{O017} describes an evolving work mix; it is not evidence that a developer loses 80\% of competence. Translate the concern into observable learning behavior rather than a second, unvalidated score: before delegating, write a prediction for one boundary case; after execution, inspect a failure or risky diff; explain the relevant invariant without reading the agent's summary; and attempt an unseen related change without assistance at the scheduled Day-14 follow-up.

nodes.label: There is a competing hypothesis. In Orosz's moderated discussion, Kent Beck argues that assistance can amplify learning \oroszcite{P123}. This is an experienced
nodes.paragraph: There is a competing hypothesis. In Orosz's moderated discussion, Kent Beck argues that assistance can amplify learning \oroszcite{P123}. This is an experienced practitioner's expectation, not a measured retention effect. Set it beside Osmani's concern: assistance might sustain prediction, explanation and experimentation, or substitute for those activities. The study should permit improvement, deterioration or no detectable difference rather than presuppose decay.

A field measurement should distinguish the arrival process from service capacity and downstream outcomes. The queueing example is deliberately deterministic, bu
nodes.paragraph: A field measurement should distinguish the arrival process from service capacity and downstream outcomes. The queueing example is deliberately deterministic, but a real team must also record task mix and variance: policy-sensitive changes may take longer to review than documentation. It should retain all candidate attempts, including those withdrawn before review, so an increase in generation cannot masquerade as an improvement in acceptance. Afroz et al.~\autocite{W094} report an estimated 519.86 additional pull requests per week across 294 sampled repositories relative to their Bayesian structural-time-series counterfactual, approximately 27,032 over 52 weeks. Their Table II also reports an estimated 1.06\% decline in aggregate PR merge ratio and an 18.18\% decline for one-time contributors. The intervention is a calendar-period proxy for the AI surge, not randomized assignment of an AI tool. It is a warning about plausible capacity pressure, not proof that AI caused every observed change.

nodes.label: The important distinction is between arrivals and accepted outcomes. Chapter~\ref{chap:02} examines how production-stage measurements can diverge; the open-sour
nodes.paragraph: The important distinction is between arrivals and accepted outcomes. Chapter~\ref{chap:02} examines how production-stage measurements can diverge; the open-source observations here suggest a capacity question for a team to test, rather than a private-company forecast. \autocite{W010,W094}

nodes.label: The queue identifies pressure, not which work may safely disappear. Nicole Forsgren and Abi Noda's guidance, excerpted alongside Orosz's interview in \emph{Fric
Hassan\textquotesingle s agentic software-engineering roadmap \autocite{W152} identifies coordination and architecture as open research problems, while Hoda\tex
nodes.paragraph: Hassan\textquotesingle s agentic software-engineering roadmap \autocite{W152} identifies coordination and architecture as open research problems, while Hoda\textquotesingle s work \autocite{W153} situates development within the social organization of software teams. These sources motivate a socio-technical account; neither proves that a seven-role chart is optimal. The proposed role model is a way to make implicit authority visible.

nodes.label: The original policy research is more nuanced than a simple percentage of projects permitting AI. Yang et al.~\autocite{W147} intentionally sampled 67 visible go
nodes.paragraph: The original policy research is more nuanced than a simple percentage of projects permitting AI. Yang et al.~\autocite{W147} intentionally sampled 67 visible governance cases---58 repositories and nine communities---using screening followed by snowball expansion. Their July 2026 arXiv v2 identifies 14 prohibitionist, 40 boundary-and-accountability, and 13 quality-first cases. The proportions are 20.9\%, 59.7\% and 19.4\% within this purposively assembled corpus, not estimates for all open-source projects. Two coders report Cohen\textquotesingle s kappa of 0.742 for dominant orientation, with macro-average kappas of 0.745 for concerns and 0.840 for strategies. These reliability statistics are author-reported and cannot be reconstructed without the coder-level labels. {[}\autocite{W147}, PDF pp.~3--5, methodology and orientation results.{]}

nodes.label: Hora et al.~\autocite{W150} studied a different unit: 281 policy documents from popular projects, plus a separate longitudinal set of 92 dedicated policy files.
nodes.paragraph: Hora et al.~\autocite{W150} studied a different unit: 281 policy documents from popular projects, plus a separate longitudinal set of 92 dedicated policy files. Their Table 1 reports 198 policies with some human-involvement guidance (70.5\%); the stricter category requiring a high level of human involvement is 67.3\%. Confusing these denominators changes the claim. Likewise, 150/281 (53.4\%) contain guidance on disclosure, but only 48.8\% make disclosure mandatory. The original manuscript labels itself submitted to ACM; it should not be cited as an accepted TOSEM article. {[}\autocite{W150}, PDF pp.~3, 7, 10--12, Tables 1--3.{]}

nodes.label: The difference between these studies matters. \autocite{W147} describes the range of strategies projects use; \autocite{W150} estimates how common selected prov
nodes.paragraph: The difference between these studies matters. \autocite{W147} describes the range of strategies projects use; \autocite{W150} estimates how common selected provisions are in its sampled policy files. Neither supplies a universal policy template or demonstrates that mandatory disclosure alone improves correctness. A written policy can change reviewer expectations without changing the quality of a generated patch.

nodes.label: Qiu and colleagues\textquotesingle{} Blueprint First, Model Second \autocite{W151} provides an architectural analogy for keeping deterministic orchestration sep
nodes.paragraph: Qiu and colleagues\textquotesingle{} Blueprint First, Model Second \autocite{W151} provides an architectural analogy for keeping deterministic orchestration separate from model-generated substeps. Its evaluation is on the TravelPlanner benchmark, not enterprise brownfield engineering. Farrag \autocite{W011} proposes specification-driven governance but reports an illustrative, noncontrolled pilot. Neither paper experimentally validates this chapter\textquotesingle s gate profile.

nodes.label: Research on agentic pull-request rejection \autocite{W071} motivates the need to understand integration failures. FlowGen\textquotesingle s process-model experi
nodes.paragraph: Research on agentic pull-request rejection \autocite{W071} motivates the need to understand integration failures. FlowGen\textquotesingle s process-model experiments \autocite{W148} concern code-generation benchmarks and should not be presented as evidence that a real team\textquotesingle s agile throughput improves under a particular agent orchestration scheme. The method must be tested against accepted changes, review time, regressions and deployment outcomes in the target environment.

nodes.label: \noindent\textbf{Ownership of the outer loop.} Osmani uses the ``outer loop'' to distinguish setting goals, judging evidence and living with outcomes from the i
nodes.paragraph: \noindent\textbf{Ownership of the outer loop.} Osmani uses the ``outer loop'' to distinguish setting goals, judging evidence and living with outcomes from the inner loop of agent-generated actions \osmanicite{O009}. The book's existing roles turn that phrase into a decision-rights contract. The policy owner authorizes \emph{what} the service should do and why; the orchestrator constrains permitted actions and stopping; an independent checker reports evidence against the authorized contract; a maintainer accepts the scoped code change; and the release owner controls deployment and rollback. The same person may hold multiple human roles in a small team, but no agent may inherit a missing approval merely by coordinating the other agents.

nodes.label: The strongest counterpoint to a purely restrictive policy is that governance itself can shape participation. Chen, Zimmermann and Trinkenreich \autocite{W149} e
nodes.paragraph: The strongest counterpoint to a purely restrictive policy is that governance itself can shape participation. Chen, Zimmermann and Trinkenreich \autocite{W149} examine 29,624 repositories and identify 385 policy adopters, using propensity-score matching and difference-in-differences. Their Table II reports changes in review activity, AI-disclosure measures and static quality proxies. But a policy requiring disclosure can alter the measurement of AI use: the authors classify AI-assisted PRs partly from observable disclosure and carry forward AI status across subsequent PRs by the same author. The treatment can therefore influence the label used for an outcome. The manuscript also contains a tension between its stated four-week post-treatment eligibility window and eight-week main-effect window. These are reasons to treat the estimates as provisional until robustness checks using direct PR-level signals and harmonized observation windows are reproduced. {[}\autocite{W149}, PDF pp.~3--4, 7--9.{]}

nodes.label: Afroz et al.~\autocite{W094} describe the risk of overwhelming open-source maintainers with plausible low-quality submissions. Asdaque and colleagues \autocite{
nodes.paragraph: Afroz et al.~\autocite{W094} describe the risk of overwhelming open-source maintainers with plausible low-quality submissions. Asdaque and colleagues \autocite{W112} study novice AI-assisted contributions and report substantial review overhead in their sample; their exact task controls and numerical tables require full-text verification before the book generalizes their ratios. Xu and colleagues\textquotesingle{} newcomer-participation work \autocite{W058} offers an important counterweight: code complexity and participation are not mechanically linked, and the causal design must be read on its own terms rather than reduced to a slogan.

nodes.label: Chapter 9 used historical turnover research (\autocite{W185} and \autocite{W173}) to motivate preserving rationale and examined why AI-generated authorship weak
nodes.paragraph: Chapter 9 used historical turnover research (\autocite{W185} and \autocite{W173}) to motivate preserving rationale and examined why AI-generated authorship weakens conventional knowledge proxies \autocite{W189}. Here we translate those concerns into a team policy. The system steward owns the dependency map and design rationale. The intent owner authorizes behavioral changes. The verification owner maintains independent oracles. The reviewer and release authority retain their decisions with source references.
